digest.discriminating_test: test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)"

root_cause.summary: The #77 fix was never applied: `src/cli/advance.ts` still builds its `--commit` staging set as `writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at both commit sites (lines 123 and 220), so companion artifacts sitting in the item's own directory but not written by this transition are left untracked behind a `gitCommitted: true`. It cannot stage the item directory because `src/process/engine.ts` never exposes one — `AdvanceResult` has no `itemDir` field and `BlockedWalkError` carries only `(message, landedOn, writtenPaths)`, so `located.dir` never leaves the engine.

digest.summary:
I read `src/cli/advance.ts` and `src/process/engine.ts` first rather than trusting the implementation report. Neither contains any trace of the change the report describes: `grep -rn itemDir src/` returns nothing, `AdvanceResult` (engine.ts:151-194) has no `itemDir`, `BlockedWalkError`'s constructor is still 3-arg, and both staging sites in advance.ts (123, 220) still pass `writtenPaths` alone. CHANGELOG.md has no #77 entry and `test/advance-git-commit.test.ts` still holds the pre-fix 'narrow staging' test the spec said to invert. Git history is a single commit — `chore(...): advance to implement` — with no fix commit at all, so the report's claimed four-file change and 10/10 test run never landed.

I confirmed the behaviour live rather than inferring it. Running the file gives 6/6 green, including the test that asserts a `_review.md` planted in the story's OWN directory stays out of the commit — the suite is currently guarding the bug, which is exactly why this failed silently. I then wrote an AC-001-shaped probe (plant the companion artifact, `advance --to g1 --commit`, assert it is committed). It fails with `expected '.bklg/foundation/cutover/root/spec.md…' to contain '_review.md'`; the commit holds only spec.md, story.md and the telemetry partition, and the companion file remains untracked. Probe deleted, working tree left clean.

The wrong behaviour ORIGINATES in advance.ts's staging-set computation, not in `src/git/index.ts` — `commit()`'s `git add -- <paths>` already recurses a directory pathspec, so no git plumbing is missing. engine.ts is named alongside it because the staging set cannot be widened without the engine surfacing `located.dir` on `AdvanceResult` and `BlockedWalkError`; those two files are the whole fix surface in `src/`. The named discriminating test is the sharpest one available: it passes today and must fail (inverted) the moment the hypothesis-implied fix exists.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` builds its git staging set as `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` (src/cli/advance.ts:121-129, and the same narrowing for `err.writtenPaths` in the BlockedWalkError catch at 219-224), so only files THIS transition wrote are staged. Companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_review.md`, a `_discovery/` corpus) are left untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. The described fix (stage `[itemDir, ...writtenPaths]`, with `AdvanceResult.itemDir` added in src/process/engine.ts) is entirely absent from this checkout.

digest.summary: Read src/cli/advance.ts, src/process/engine.ts (AdvanceResult/BlockedWalkError/locateItemIn), src/git/index.ts commit(), and test/advance-git-commit.test.ts. grep showed no `itemDir` anywhere in src/, the test file still has its original 6 tests (including the un-inverted 'narrow staging' test), the on-disk implementation-report.md is the unauthored template, and CHANGELOG.md has no #77 entry — the claimed implementation never landed. I then ran the existing suite (6/6 green, including the narrow-staging assertion) and wrote a throwaway repro test: planting `_review.md` in the item's own directory and running `advance --to g1 --commit --json` yields `gitCommitted: true` while the commit contains only spec.md + story.md + the telemetry partition (exactly writtenPaths) and `_review.md` stays `??` untracked. A sibling item's stray file correctly stays out, so the boundary is not the issue — the staging set is. git/index.ts's commit() is correct (it stages whatever pathspecs it is given, directories included) and engine.ts's writtenPaths is correct by its own definition; the wrong behaviour originates where the CLI chooses the pathspec list.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` builds its git staging set as `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` (src/cli/advance.ts:121-129, and the same narrowing for `err.writtenPaths` in the BlockedWalkError catch at 219-224), so only files THIS transition wrote are staged. Companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_review.md`, a `_discovery/` corpus) are left untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. The described fix (stage `[itemDir, ...writtenPaths]`, with `AdvanceResult.itemDir` added in src/process/engine.ts) is entirely absent from this checkout.

structured_output.summary: Read src/cli/advance.ts, src/process/engine.ts (AdvanceResult/BlockedWalkError/locateItemIn), src/git/index.ts commit(), and test/advance-git-commit.test.ts. grep showed no `itemDir` anywhere in src/, the test file still has its original 6 tests (including the un-inverted 'narrow staging' test), the on-disk implementation-report.md is the unauthored template, and CHANGELOG.md has no #77 entry — the claimed implementation never landed. I then ran the existing suite (6/6 green, including the narrow-staging assertion) and wrote a throwaway repro test: planting `_review.md` in the item's own directory and running `advance --to g1 --commit --json` yields `gitCommitted: true` while the commit contains only spec.md + story.md + the telemetry partition (exactly writtenPaths) and `_review.md` stays `??` untracked. A sibling item's stray file correctly stays out, so the boundary is not the issue — the staging set is. git/index.ts's commit() is correct (it stages whatever pathspecs it is given, directories included) and engine.ts's writtenPaths is correct by its own definition; the wrong behaviour originates where the CLI chooses the pathspec list.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test does not exist in this checkout, so its "pass" is produced by zero tests running and is identical whether or not the fix landed.
findings.rationale: I ran the exact test-name filter with correct quoting and watched vitest collect the file, match nothing, skip all 6 tests and exit 0. I also confirmed by grep that no test with that name exists. This is an observed behaviour of the proposed discriminator, not an inference.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "sweeps a companion artifact already in the item's own directory into the commit"  # plus: grep -rn "sweeps a companion" test/
repro.expected_when_met: A genuine discriminator would run exactly one test and change outcome between worlds: 1 passed with the fix present, 1 failed (or 0 matched) without it. Here both worlds yield exit 0, so the observation carries no information about the staging policy.
repro.observed: 'test/advance-git-commit.test.ts (6 tests | 6 skipped)' / 'Test Files 1 skipped (1)' / 'Tests 6 skipped (6)', EXIT=0. grep for the test name returns no match anywhere in test/ or src/. The run recorded by the investigator (unquoted -t) applied no filter at all: it reports '92 passed (92)' test files and '1877 passed (1877)' tests in 215s, i.e. the whole suite.

findings.claim: The only test standing for the staging boundary is misnamed: 'does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)' plants its file in the item's OWN directory, so it pins the buggy narrow-staging policy rather than the boundary its name promises.
findings.rationale: The test name asserts a boundary requirement (a sibling/unrelated file stays out) but the body writes to storyDir() — the advancing item's own directory — which is exactly the shape the issue reports as broken. I confirmed the gap by mutation: under a broadened staging patch this test FAILS while a file placed in a genuinely different item directory still stays out, so it is pinning the defect, not the boundary. No test covering AC-002 (a different item's untracked file) exists.

repro.command: sed -n '188,201p' test/advance-git-commit.test.ts; # then patch src/cli/advance.ts:123 to stage [dirname(itemFile), ...writtenPaths] and: npx vitest run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts test/zz-review-repro.test.ts
repro.expected_when_met: A test named for the boundary would place the stray file OUTSIDE the advancing item's directory and keep passing under both the narrow and the broadened staging policy; a separate, differently-named test would cover the in-directory companion case.
repro.observed: Body is `writeFileSync(join(storyDir(), "_review.md"), ...)` where storyDir() = .bklg/foundation/cutover/root — the advancing story's own directory. Unpatched: 6/6 pass. Patched: that test FAILS ('expected ... not to contain "_review.md"', committed set now includes .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_review.md), while my sibling-directory probe (.bklg/foundation/cutover/_sibling-stray.md) still passes — committed set is spec.md, story.md, telemetry only.

findings.claim: advance --commit reports gitCommitted:true while leaving companion artifacts that already sit in the item's own directory (_review.md, a _discovery/ corpus) untracked — the behaviour originates in the pathspec list built in src/cli/advance.ts, not in git/index.ts or engine.ts.
findings.rationale: I ran the CLI end to end in an isolated git repo and read the resulting commit and git status, then established causality by mutation: changing only src/cli/advance.ts's staging set (no engine.ts, no git/index.ts change) flipped the outcome, so the wrong value is computed at that site rather than merely surfaced there.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-review-repro.test.ts  # throwaway: plant _review.md and _discovery/notes.md in the story dir, then `advance <id> --to g1 --commit --json`
repro.expected_when_met: The commit produced by `advance --commit` would list the companion _review.md and _discovery/notes.md alongside spec.md/story.md, and `git status --porcelain -- .bklg` would be empty.
repro.observed: GITCOMMITTED=true SHA=99ea63a3...; COMMITTED_FILES = .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/spec.md | .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/story.md | .redkiln/telemetry/events/ryan@....jsonl; STATUS = ?? .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_discovery/ | ?? .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_review.md. After patching ONLY src/cli/advance.ts:123 to prepend dirname(itemFile), the same run committed _review.md and _discovery/notes.md as well. grep shows no `itemDir` anywhere in src/; dist/cli.js:15762 carries the same `writtenPaths.filter` staging.

findings.claim: The proposed fix's sanctioned change set is wider than the single file named: src/process/engine.ts (AdvanceResult.itemDir), the test file, and CHANGELOG.md are all part of the frozen boundary, and none of them are touched.
findings.rationale: This is a completeness note about the actionable change set, not a defect in the root-cause location. My mutation showed a one-file edit in src/cli/advance.ts is causally sufficient to change the behaviour, so naming that file as the origin is correct; I cannot evidence that omitting engine.ts from the `files` list makes the root cause wrong, only that the fix as specced spans more files.

repro.command: grep -rn "itemDir" src/ ; grep -n "77" CHANGELOG.md ; sed -n '150,195p' src/process/engine.ts
repro.expected_when_met: AdvanceResult would carry `readonly itemDir: string` populated from located.dir at all construction sites, advance.ts would stage [result.itemDir, ...writtenPaths], and CHANGELOG.md would carry an Unreleased entry naming the behaviour change.
repro.observed: No `itemDir` occurrence anywhere under src/ (only unrelated helper functions in test/). CHANGELOG.md contains no reference to #77. AdvanceResult declares id/from/to/status/committed/paused/gate/writtenPaths/advisories and no itemDir; its doc comment still states 'The CLI stages EXACTLY these'. The telemetry partition in writtenPaths sits outside the item directory, so an itemDir-only staging would drop it — AC-003 depends on the additive [itemDir, ...writtenPaths] form.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001..AC-005 are satisfied by a change: AC-001's companion-artifact sweep is absent (reproduced: commit contains only spec.md/story.md/telemetry while _review.md and _discovery/ stay untracked behind gitCommitted:true), AC-002's sibling-boundary test does not exist, and AC-003/004/005 are green only vacuously because nothing changed. No itemDir in src/, no CHANGELOG #77 entry, dist/ carries the same narrow staging.

`git status --porcelain` is empty and `git diff --stat` shows nothing: no file inside or outside the frozen boundary was modified. My own experimental patch to src/cli/advance.ts and the throwaway test were both reverted/removed and verified clean. Trivially faithful, since nothing was touched at all.

The suite is honest in the sense that no assertion was weakened or skipped, but test/advance-git-commit.test.ts:188 is misnamed — it advertises 'unrelated untracked sibling' while planting the file in the advancing item's OWN directory (storyDir()), so the one test standing for the boundary actually pins the defect. I confirmed by mutation that it fails the moment the correct behaviour is implemented, and that no test covers the real boundary (a different item's directory).

The recorded full run is 92/92 files and 1877/1877 tests green, and I independently re-ran test/advance-git-commit.test.ts to 6/6 green in 10s. The greenness is real but uninformative: it is green because the implementation never changed. I did not run typecheck or lint myself, so that part of the merge gate is unverified.

Zero regression risk because zero production code changed — HEAD and the working tree are identical. The corollary is that the shipped behaviour, including the untracked-companion state that issue #76's verifier reportedly trips over, is entirely unchanged; risk is low only in the sense that nothing was delivered.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` builds its git staging set as `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` (src/cli/advance.ts:121-129, and the same narrowing for `err.writtenPaths` in the BlockedWalkError catch at 219-224), so only files THIS transition wrote are staged. Companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_review.md`, a `_discovery/` corpus) are left untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. The described fix (stage `[itemDir, ...writtenPaths]`, with `AdvanceResult.itemDir` added in src/process/engine.ts) is entirely absent from this checkout.

hypothesis.summary: Read src/cli/advance.ts, src/process/engine.ts (AdvanceResult/BlockedWalkError/locateItemIn), src/git/index.ts commit(), and test/advance-git-commit.test.ts. grep showed no `itemDir` anywhere in src/, the test file still has its original 6 tests (including the un-inverted 'narrow staging' test), the on-disk implementation-report.md is the unauthored template, and CHANGELOG.md has no #77 entry — the claimed implementation never landed. I then ran the existing suite (6/6 green, including the narrow-staging assertion) and wrote a throwaway repro test: planting `_review.md` in the item's own directory and running `advance --to g1 --commit --json` yields `gitCommitted: true` while the commit contains only spec.md + story.md + the telemetry partition (exactly writtenPaths) and `_review.md` stays `??` untracked. A sibling item's stray file correctly stays out, so the boundary is not the issue — the staging set is. git/index.ts's commit() is correct (it stages whatever pathspecs it is given, directories included) and engine.ts's writtenPaths is correct by its own definition; the wrong behaviour originates where the CLI chooses the pathspec list.

digest.discriminating_test: test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)"

root_cause.summary: The #77 fix was never implemented in this checkout: `src/cli/advance.ts` still stages only `result.writtenPaths` (line 123) and `err.writtenPaths` (line 220, the BlockedWalkError catch), so companion artifacts sitting in the item's own directory but not written by this transition are left untracked behind a commit reporting `gitCommitted: true`. The enabling gap is in `src/process/engine.ts`, where `AdvanceResult` and `BlockedWalkError` still carry no `itemDir` field (`located.dir`, resolved at engine.ts:752, is never surfaced), so the CLI has no item-directory pathspec to stage.

digest.summary: I read src/cli/advance.ts, src/process/engine.ts and src/git/index.ts before forming a view. `grep -rn itemDir src/` returns nothing: AdvanceResult has only `writtenPaths` (engine.ts:184) with a doc comment still promising the commit 'never sweeps in unrelated files', BlockedWalkError (engine.ts:213-224) likewise, and `located.dir` (engine.ts:752) is never exported on the result. Both commit sites in src/cli/advance.ts (lines 123 and 220) still pass `writtenPaths` alone to gitCommit. test/advance-git-commit.test.ts still holds the un-inverted 'narrow staging' test and none of the six new tests the report tables; CHANGELOG has no #77 Unreleased entry; the in-repo implementation-report.md is the blank unauthored template. I ran `npx vitest run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts`: 6 tests pass (report claimed 10/10), including the narrow-staging test, which plants `_review.md` in storyDir() — the item's OWN directory, AC-001's exact scenario — and asserts it stays OUT of the commit and untracked. That green assertion is the #77 symptom reproduced directly. src/git/index.ts's commit() is not at fault: its `git add -- <paths>` already accepts a directory pathspec, it is simply never handed one. The discriminating test is that same named test: it passes on the current tree and would necessarily fail (it is the test the fix inverts) if the shipped implementation existed.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` stages only the transition's own `writtenPaths` — `src/cli/advance.ts:123` (success path) and `:220` (BlockedWalkError path) — so companion artifacts already present in the item's directory are never staged; the enabling gap is that `AdvanceResult` and `BlockedWalkError` in `src/process/engine.ts` carry no `itemDir` field to stage. digest.summary: The #77 fix was never implemented despite the implementation report claiming it shipped. `src/cli/advance.ts` still stages `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at its success commit site (:123) and `err.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at the BlockedWalkError catch (:220) — no item-directory pathspec — so companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory stay untracked behind a commit reporting `gitCommitted: true`. `src/process/engine.ts` never gained the `itemDir` field on `AdvanceResult` (:177-184) or `BlockedWalkError` (:216-221), so the CLI has nothing to stage even if it wanted to (`grep -rn itemDir src/` = 0 hits). I reproduced the symptom: `vitest run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts` gives 6 tests (report claims 10), and the un-inverted "does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)" test still PASSES — a `_review.md` planted in the story's own dir is absent from the commit and left `??` in git status, which is exactly the #77 defect. CHANGELOG's Unreleased/Fixed has #66 and #62 but no #77 entry, and the item's own implementation-report.md on disk is the unauthored template. Sibling fixtures for later items (issue-79, issue-137) do carry `itemDir`, so this is a genuine absence, not a pre-fix baseline.

digest.discriminating_test: test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "narrow staging"

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` builds its staging set from the transition's own writes only — `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at src/cli/advance.ts:123 and `err.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at src/cli/advance.ts:220 — so a companion artifact already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_review.md`, a `_discovery/` corpus) is never staged and stays untracked behind a commit that reports success. The RK-S0234 fix (an `itemDir` field on `AdvanceResult`/`BlockedWalkError` sourced from `located.dir`, staged as `[itemDir, ...writtenPaths]`) is entirely absent from this checkout: no `itemDir` anywhere in `src/`, the "narrow staging" test un-inverted and green, and no #77 CHANGELOG entry.

digest.summary: Read src/cli/advance.ts, src/process/engine.ts and src/git/index.ts before forming a view. The staging set for a `--commit` advance is chosen in advance.ts (line 123 for the normal path, line 220 in the BlockedWalkError catch) and is `writtenPaths` alone; `commit()` in src/git/index.ts stages faithfully whatever pathspecs it is given (and already accepts directories), and `writtenPaths` is correct for what it means, so neither is the origin. I then ran `npx vitest run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts`: 6/6 green, including \"does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)\", which plants `_review.md` in the STORY'S OWN directory, advances with `--commit`, and asserts the file is absent from the commit and still untracked — i.e. the #77 symptom reproduced and asserted as intended behaviour. Grep confirms `itemDir` appears nowhere in `src/`, `AdvanceResult` and `BlockedWalkError` have no such field, CHANGELOG's Unreleased section has no #77 entry, and the test the spec required to be inverted is untouched — so all four files of the frozen boundary are at pre-fix contents and the reported implementation is not present. (Cross-check against the sibling `e3-clean-issue-77-*` fixture, which does contain the fix, rules out a renamed-field implementation.) The discriminating test is the AC-001 shape: plant a companion artifact in the item's directory, run `advance --commit`, assert `git show --stat` contains it — it fails today and passes once advance.ts stages `[itemDir, ...writtenPaths]`; if the defect instead lived in `commit()` or in `writtenPaths` collection, that test would not flip on an advance.ts-only change.

digest.discriminating_test: test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts (AC-001: "enters withWriteLock exactly once, and the real shell-out runs while UNLOCKED"). The file is absent; the equivalent probe I wrote and ran - a gate script that checks whether <git-common-dir>/redkiln/.write.lock exists at invocation, driven by one `advance <id> --apply` over a `{{redkiln}} verify --grain story` gate - records ["locked"] on this tree and would record ["unlocked"] once advance() pre-flights the gate outside the lock.

root_cause.summary: advance() in src/process/engine.ts (lines 769-772) wraps the entire advanceUnlocked call - including evaluateGate at line 1157 and its synchronous execFileSync command-gate shell-out - in withWriteLock, so a repo-wide lock is held for the full runtime of the merge-gate suite. The spec's remedy (an unlocked pre-flight pass plus a preflightOnly field on AdvanceOptions) was never implemented; the function and the AdvanceOptions interface in this same file are unchanged.

digest.summary: The fix described by RK-S0263 was never applied. The repo has one commit ("advance to implement") and advance() in src/process/engine.ts:769-772 is still the pre-fix form quoted by the spec: `if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts); return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts));`. `preflightOnly` appears nowhere in src/ (grep count 0); none of the four claimed helpers (headResolves, gateMemoUsable, isMemoizedVerifyGate, preflightStage) exist; test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist; CHANGELOG.md has no Unreleased entry for it; and dist/cli.js and dist/index.js both still carry the pre-fix line at 14969 (consistent with src, so this is not a stale-bundle issue). The on-disk implementation-report.md is the unauthored template stub, so the narrative report was never committed either. I reproduced the underlying defect directly: a probe verify.affected_gate script that records whether the shared write-lock directory exists when it fires logged ["locked"] across one `advance <story> --apply` through the implement command gate - i.e. the gate's shell-out runs INSIDE the shared cross-worktree write lock, exactly what AC-001 forbids. The lock's cross-worktree path (coordinationDir in src/store/lock.ts) is correct and out of scope, and gates.ts / verify-cache.ts need no change; the scope error is solely in how advance() composes them.

I verified the behaviour rather than inferring it: I wrote a probe test that drives a story to plan under a verify --grain story gate whose affected_gate script records whether the shared write-lock directory exists at shell-out time. Passing gate produced log "L" (the real run happened while the lock was held); failing gate produced "LL" (two real runs, both inside the lock, so withWriteLock was entered for a blocked advance, violating AC-002). hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts (AC-001: "enters withWriteLock exactly once, and the real shell-out runs while UNLOCKED"). The file is absent; the equivalent probe I wrote and ran - a gate script that checks whether <git-common-dir>/redkiln/.write.lock exists at invocation, driven by one `advance <id> --apply` over a `{{redkiln}} verify --grain story` gate - records ["locked"] on this tree and would record ["unlocked"] once advance() pre-flights the gate outside the lock.

root_cause.summary: advance() in src/process/engine.ts (lines 769-772) wraps the entire advanceUnlocked call - including evaluateGate at line 1157 and its synchronous execFileSync command-gate shell-out - in withWriteLock, so a repo-wide lock is held for the full runtime of the merge-gate suite. The spec's remedy (an unlocked pre-flight pass plus a preflightOnly field on AdvanceOptions) was never implemented; the function and the AdvanceOptions interface in this same file are unchanged.

hypothesis.summary: The fix described by RK-S0263 was never applied. The repo has one commit ("advance to implement") and advance() in src/process/engine.ts:769-772 is still the pre-fix form quoted by the spec: `if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts); return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts));`. `preflightOnly` appears nowhere in src/ (grep count 0); none of the four claimed helpers (headResolves, gateMemoUsable, isMemoizedVerifyGate, preflightStage) exist; test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist; CHANGELOG.md has no Unreleased entry for it; and dist/cli.js and dist/index.js both still carry the pre-fix line at 14969 (consistent with src, so this is not a stale-bundle issue). The on-disk implementation-report.md is the unauthored template stub, so the narrative report was never committed either. I reproduced the underlying defect directly: a probe verify.affected_gate script that records whether the shared write-lock directory exists when it fires logged ["locked"] across one `advance <story> --apply` through the implement command gate - i.e. the gate's shell-out runs INSIDE the shared cross-worktree write lock, exactly what AC-001 forbids. The lock's cross-worktree path (coordinationDir in src/store/lock.ts) is correct and out of scope, and gates.ts / verify-cache.ts need no change; the scope error is solely in how advance() composes them.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test cannot distinguish "fix absent" from "fix landed as specified": as issued it applies no filter at all and times out, and when issued correctly it exits 0 in both worlds because the spec mandates renaming that very test.
findings.rationale: I ran both halves and watched the outcomes: the pnpm form ran unrelated test files (no filter applied) and had to be killed, and a name pattern that matches nothing exits 0 with all tests skipped — so a "PASSES" observation is produced by the fixed world too. This is direct observation, not inference.

repro.command: pnpm test -- --run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t narrow staging   # then: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "stages the item directory (broad staging)"
repro.expected_when_met: A command whose exit status differs between the fault-present and fault-fixed states — e.g. the investigator's own positive probe (`_review.md` asserted PRESENT in `git show --stat`), which fails today and passes under the fix, or an isolated quoted invocation of an assertion that survives the rename.
repro.observed: (a) pnpm expands to `vitest run "--" "--run" "test/advance-git-commit.test.ts" "-t" "narrow" "staging"`; the literal `--` sends every filter into cac's `--` bucket, so NO filter is applied and the full suite runs (observed test/workflow-model-tiers.test.ts, test/implement-contract.test.ts, test/index-build.test.ts, test/upgrade-command.test.ts executing); I killed it, matching the harness's 420s kill. (b) Quoted and isolated, `-t "narrow staging"` runs 1 test, passes, exit 0 in 30s. (c) With the name pattern the spec's own boundary row mandates ('invert/rename'), vitest reports `Test Files 1 skipped (1) / Tests 6 skipped (6)` and exits 0 — a pass.

findings.claim: The fix the investigator validated leaves the second staging site they name (`src/cli/advance.ts:220`, the BlockedWalkError catch) untouched, so `advance --to <stage> --commit` blocked partway still commits without the companion artifact.
findings.rationale: I applied the exact described fix (`itemDir` on `AdvanceResult` at all 7 return sites + `[result.itemDir, ...writtenPaths]` at :123, `tsc --noEmit` clean) and ran a blocked-walk probe: the commit for the cleared hop still omits `_review.md`, which remains `??`. Their probe only exercised the single-step path, so it cannot support the part of the claim that names :220.

repro.command: scratch patch (itemDir on AdvanceResult + `[result.itemDir, ...writtenPaths]` at advance.ts:123) + probe: 4-stage 'walkdeep' process (impl -> build passes, integ blocks), `_review.md` planted in the story dir, `advance <id> --to review --commit`
repro.expected_when_met: The blocked-walk commit contains `_review.md` too — i.e. the BlockedWalkError path also carries and stages the item directory, since AC-001's WHEN is `advance --commit`, not `advance --commit that did not block`.
repro.observed: exit non-zero (gate blocked), one commit created for the cleared hop containing `.bklg/.../_integration.md`, `.bklg/.../story.md`, telemetry — `_review.md` absent from the commit and still `?? .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_review.md`. Identical before and after the patch.

findings.claim: `src/process/engine.ts` is named as a root-cause file but contains no defect: the fault is fully removed by a change confined to `src/cli/advance.ts`, so the engine edit is the chosen fix shape, not the origin.
findings.rationale: I patched only `src/cli/advance.ts` (staging the directory of each written `.bklg` path alongside `writtenPaths`, no engine change at all) and the AC-001/AC-002/AC-003 probes all went green. The engine correctly reports what the transition wrote — the spec itself says `writtenPaths`' meaning is unchanged — so listing engine.ts under `root_cause.files` widens the causal locus beyond what the fault requires.

repro.expected_when_met: A root-cause file set in which every named file contains code that must change for the fault to stop — no file that is only implicated by a preferred fix shape.
repro.observed: 3 passed: companion `_review.md` IS in the commit, a sibling item's `_sibling.md` stays out and untracked, telemetry partition still committed — with src/process/engine.ts byte-identical to HEAD.

findings.claim: The test that the root cause treats as the current boundary guard does not test that boundary: 'does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)' plants its file in the item's OWN directory, so nothing in the suite pins the sibling-item boundary AC-002 stands for.
findings.rationale: The test name promises sibling/unrelated-file coverage but line 192 writes to `storyDir()` — the item's own directory. My probe shows the two cases behave differently under the fix (own-dir file gets swept in, sibling's does not), so the existing test pins strictly less than its name claims and, once inverted, leaves AC-002 unguarded until the new test is written.

repro.command: read test/advance-git-commit.test.ts:188-201; grep -n "_sibling\|siblingDir" test/
repro.expected_when_met: A test that seeds a second item, plants an untracked file in that item's directory, advances the first item with --commit, and asserts the sibling's file is absent from `git show --name-only` and still present in `git status --porcelain`.
repro.observed: The only nearby assertion writes `_review.md` into `join(work, ".bklg", "foundation", "cutover", "root")` — the advanced story's own dir. No test anywhere plants an untracked file in a DIFFERENT item's directory, so the sibling boundary is currently unpinned in both the pre- and post-fix worlds.

findings.claim: The 'all 8 construction sites' framing of the engine.ts anchor is off by one: there are 7 `AdvanceResult` return sites; the 8th `writtenPaths` grep hit is the positional `BlockedWalkError` constructor argument, which the described fix never populates.
findings.rationale: I observed `tsc --noEmit` pass cleanly after adding `itemDir` at exactly 7 return sites (engine.ts 842/879/927/983/1038/1343/1388), which shows the 8th hit is not an AdvanceResult site — but this is a precision complaint about the anchor list rather than a behavioural failure I can pin to an AC on its own, so I am not inflating it above advisory.

repro.command: grep -n "writtenPaths" src/process/engine.ts; node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit (after adding itemDir at the 7 return sites)
repro.expected_when_met: An anchor list whose site count matches the code, with the BlockedWalkError carrier called out separately as a site the fix must also feed (see the blocked-walk finding).
repro.observed: 7 AdvanceResult literals carry `writtenPaths:`; line 1318 is `new BlockedWalkError(..., [...writtenPaths])`. Typecheck is clean with 7 additions, i.e. the compiler agrees there is no 8th AdvanceResult site.

rubric.rationale: The claim correctly localises AC-001's single-step path (I reproduced the symptom and watched a two-file patch flip it), but the validated fix does not cover the blocked-walk `--commit` path the claim itself names, and AC-002's boundary is asserted rather than evidenced by any test that actually plants a sibling file.

The repo is clean at HEAD — the investigator left no residue from their scratch patch — and every file they name (`src/cli/advance.ts`, `src/process/engine.ts`) sits inside the spec's frozen boundary. They correctly refused to implicate `src/git/index.ts`, which I confirmed already stages directories unchanged.

The named discriminating test is inert: unquoted through pnpm it applies no filter at all, and under the rename the spec itself mandates it exits 0 with every test skipped, so 'currently PASSES' is produced by both the buggy and the fixed world. The investigator's own throwaway probe was sound, but it is not the test recorded as the discriminator.

The recorded gate run produced no signal — it swept the entire suite and was killed at 420s, which I reproduced exactly. The one gate I could run cleanly (`tsc --noEmit` under the scratch patch) was green, so the failure is in how the gate was invoked, not in the tree.

The staging change is well-bounded — I confirmed a sibling item's untracked file stays out and the telemetry partition and the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression both survive — but the un-addressed BlockedWalkError path means a fixer following this root cause ships a half-fix, and the unguarded sibling boundary means that half-fix regresses silently.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test cannot distinguish "fix absent" from "fix landed as specified": as issued it applies no filter at all and times out, and when issued correctly it exits 0 in both worlds because the spec mandates renaming that very test.
findings.rationale: I ran both halves and watched the outcomes: the pnpm form ran unrelated test files (no filter applied) and had to be killed, and a name pattern that matches nothing exits 0 with all tests skipped — so a "PASSES" observation is produced by the fixed world too. This is direct observation, not inference.

repro.command: pnpm test -- --run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t narrow staging   # then: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "stages the item directory (broad staging)"
repro.expected_when_met: A command whose exit status differs between the fault-present and fault-fixed states — e.g. the investigator's own positive probe (`_review.md` asserted PRESENT in `git show --stat`), which fails today and passes under the fix, or an isolated quoted invocation of an assertion that survives the rename.
repro.observed: (a) pnpm expands to `vitest run "--" "--run" "test/advance-git-commit.test.ts" "-t" "narrow" "staging"`; the literal `--` sends every filter into cac's `--` bucket, so NO filter is applied and the full suite runs (observed test/workflow-model-tiers.test.ts, test/implement-contract.test.ts, test/index-build.test.ts, test/upgrade-command.test.ts executing); I killed it, matching the harness's 420s kill. (b) Quoted and isolated, `-t "narrow staging"` runs 1 test, passes, exit 0 in 30s. (c) With the name pattern the spec's own boundary row mandates ('invert/rename'), vitest reports `Test Files 1 skipped (1) / Tests 6 skipped (6)` and exits 0 — a pass.

findings.claim: The fix the investigator validated leaves the second staging site they name (`src/cli/advance.ts:220`, the BlockedWalkError catch) untouched, so `advance --to <stage> --commit` blocked partway still commits without the companion artifact.
findings.rationale: I applied the exact described fix (`itemDir` on `AdvanceResult` at all 7 return sites + `[result.itemDir, ...writtenPaths]` at :123, `tsc --noEmit` clean) and ran a blocked-walk probe: the commit for the cleared hop still omits `_review.md`, which remains `??`. Their probe only exercised the single-step path, so it cannot support the part of the claim that names :220.

repro.command: scratch patch (itemDir on AdvanceResult + `[result.itemDir, ...writtenPaths]` at advance.ts:123) + probe: 4-stage 'walkdeep' process (impl -> build passes, integ blocks), `_review.md` planted in the story dir, `advance <id> --to review --commit`
repro.expected_when_met: The blocked-walk commit contains `_review.md` too — i.e. the BlockedWalkError path also carries and stages the item directory, since AC-001's WHEN is `advance --commit`, not `advance --commit that did not block`.
repro.observed: exit non-zero (gate blocked), one commit created for the cleared hop containing `.bklg/.../_integration.md`, `.bklg/.../story.md`, telemetry — `_review.md` absent from the commit and still `?? .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_review.md`. Identical before and after the patch.

findings.claim: `src/process/engine.ts` is named as a root-cause file but contains no defect: the fault is fully removed by a change confined to `src/cli/advance.ts`, so the engine edit is the chosen fix shape, not the origin.
findings.rationale: I patched only `src/cli/advance.ts` (staging the directory of each written `.bklg` path alongside `writtenPaths`, no engine change at all) and the AC-001/AC-002/AC-003 probes all went green. The engine correctly reports what the transition wrote — the spec itself says `writtenPaths`' meaning is unchanged — so listing engine.ts under `root_cause.files` widens the causal locus beyond what the fault requires.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test cannot distinguish "fix absent" from "fix landed as specified": as issued it applies no filter at all and times out, and when issued correctly it exits 0 in both worlds because the spec mandates renaming that very test.
findings.rationale: I ran both halves and watched the outcomes: the pnpm form ran unrelated test files (no filter applied) and had to be killed, and a name pattern that matches nothing exits 0 with all tests skipped — so a "PASSES" observation is produced by the fixed world too. This is direct observation, not inference.

repro.command: pnpm test -- --run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t narrow staging   # then: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "stages the item directory (broad staging)"
repro.expected_when_met: A command whose exit status differs between the fault-present and fault-fixed states — e.g. the investigator's own positive probe (`_review.md` asserted PRESENT in `git show --stat`), which fails today and passes under the fix, or an isolated quoted invocation of an assertion that survives the rename.
repro.observed: (a) pnpm expands to `vitest run "--" "--run" "test/advance-git-commit.test.ts" "-t" "narrow" "staging"`; the literal `--` sends every filter into cac's `--` bucket, so NO filter is applied and the full suite runs (observed test/workflow-model-tiers.test.ts, test/implement-contract.test.ts, test/index-build.test.ts, test/upgrade-command.test.ts executing); I killed it, matching the harness's 420s kill. (b) Quoted and isolated, `-t "narrow staging"` runs 1 test, passes, exit 0 in 30s. (c) With the name pattern the spec's own boundary row mandates ('invert/rename'), vitest reports `Test Files 1 skipped (1) / Tests 6 skipped (6)` and exits 0 — a pass.

My probe shows the two cases behave differently under the fix (own-dir file gets swept in, sibling's does not), so the existing test pins strictly less than its name claims and, once inverted, leaves AC-002 unguarded until the new test is written.

repro.expected_when_met: A test that seeds a second item, plants an untracked file in that item's directory, advances the first item with --commit, and asserts the sibling's file is absent from `git show --name-only` and still present in `git status --porcelain`.

findings.claim: The 'all 8 construction sites' framing of the engine.ts anchor is off by one: there are 7 `AdvanceResult` return sites; the 8th `writtenPaths` grep hit is the positional `BlockedWalkError` constructor argument, which the described fix never populates.
findings.rationale: I observed `tsc --noEmit` pass cleanly after adding `itemDir` at exactly 7 return sites (engine.ts 842/879/927/983/1038/1343/1388), which shows the 8th hit is not an AdvanceResult site — but this is a precision complaint about the anchor list rather than a behavioural failure I can pin to an AC on its own, so I am not inflating it above advisory.

repro.command: grep -n "writtenPaths" src/process/engine.ts; node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit (after adding itemDir at the 7 return sites)
repro.expected_when_met: An anchor list whose site count matches the code, with the BlockedWalkError carrier called out separately as a site the fix must also feed (see the blocked-walk finding).
repro.observed: 7 AdvanceResult literals carry `writtenPaths:`; line 1318 is `new BlockedWalkError(..., [...writtenPaths])`. Typecheck is clean with 7 additions, i.e. the compiler agrees there is no 8th AdvanceResult site.

rubric.rationale: The claim correctly localises AC-001's single-step path (I reproduced the symptom and watched a two-file patch flip it), but the validated fix does not cover the blocked-walk `--commit` path the claim itself names, and AC-002's boundary is asserted rather than evidenced by any test that actually plants a sibling file.

The repo is clean at HEAD — the investigator left no residue from their scratch patch — and every file they name (`src/cli/advance.ts`, `src/process/engine.ts`) sits inside the spec's frozen boundary. They correctly refused to implicate `src/git/index.ts`, which I confirmed already stages directories unchanged.

The named discriminating test is inert: unquoted through pnpm it applies no filter at all, and under the rename the spec itself mandates it exits 0 with every test skipped, so 'currently PASSES' is produced by both the buggy and the fixed world. The investigator's own throwaway probe was sound, but it is not the test recorded as the discriminator.

The recorded gate run produced no signal — it swept the entire suite and was killed at 420s, which I reproduced exactly. The one gate I could run cleanly (`tsc --noEmit` under the scratch patch) was green, so the failure is in how the gate was invoked, not in the tree.

The staging change is well-bounded — I confirmed a sibling item's untracked file stays out and the telemetry partition and the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression both survive — but the un-addressed BlockedWalkError path means a fixer following this root cause ships a half-fix, and the unguarded sibling boundary means that half-fix regresses silently.

digest.discriminating_test: test/plan-dag.test.ts — a DigestPatch case on a clean acyclic seed rewriting the `verify-plan` digest to `{pass: true, planWritten: false}` (and a second forcing the fix pass so `re-verify:plan` reports `{pass: true, planWritten: false}`), asserting `m.verified === false`. I ran exactly this as a scratch file (test/zz-probe-issue79.test.ts, since deleted) and observed `verified: true` in both cases.

root_cause.summary: workflows/forge-plan-prds.js still computes the manifest's `verified` from the verify agent's self-reported `pass` alone (`const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`, line 1241), and neither VERIFY_SCHEMA (line 546, no `planWritten` field) nor the `verify-plan`/`re-verify:plan` prompts require a mechanical `test -f`/read check that `_plan.md` was actually authored — so a run reports `verified: true` over an unwritten rollup. None of the described fix was applied to this file.

digest.summary: The reported fix for #79 was never applied. `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` is still in its exact pre-fix state: `VERIFY_SCHEMA` (line 546) is `required: ['pass','planPath','gaps']` with no `planWritten`; the `verify-plan` (~1119-1137) and `re-verify:plan` (~1219-1221) prompts carry no rollup postcondition ("ROLLUP POSTCONDITION", `test -f ${PLAN_PATH}`) — the string appears nowhere in the repo; and line 1241 is still `const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`. `grep -ri planwritten` over the whole tree matches only the spec document. The report's own line citations (`:1276-1277` for `verified`, `:1261` for `verdict = reVerdict`) don't exist — the real file is ~27 lines shorter, i.e. it never grew. I confirmed the behaviour directly with a temporary probe test using the harness's pre-existing `DigestPatch`: on a clean acyclic gap-free seed, patching the `verify-plan` digest to `pass:true, planWritten:false` yields `m.verified === true` (AC-001 demands false), and forcing the fix-pass path with `re-verify:plan` reporting `pass:true, planWritten:false` also yields `m.verified === true` (AC-003 demands false). The dispatched verify schema's `required` array has no `planWritten`. The defect is silent because the guarding tests were never added either: `vitest run test/plan-dag.test.ts` passes 21/21, not the 25/25 the report claims, and there is no `AC-PW` describe block, no `patch` parameter on `run()`, no `planWritten` in `digestFor`, and no #79 entry in CHANGELOG (it appears only as a cross-reference inside the #73 entry). The defect therefore lives where the issue said it did — the verify/rollup step of forge-plan-prds.js, which derives a filesystem fact (`_plan.md` was authored) from the agent's own unverified `pass` flag.

structured_output.discriminating_test: test/plan-dag.test.ts — a DigestPatch case on a clean acyclic seed rewriting the `verify-plan` digest to `{pass: true, planWritten: false}` (and a second forcing the fix pass so `re-verify:plan` reports `{pass: true, planWritten: false}`), asserting `m.verified === false`. I ran exactly this as a scratch file (test/zz-probe-issue79.test.ts, since deleted) and observed `verified: true` in both cases.

root_cause.summary: workflows/forge-plan-prds.js still computes the manifest's `verified` from the verify agent's self-reported `pass` alone (`const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`, line 1241), and neither VERIFY_SCHEMA (line 546, no `planWritten` field) nor the `verify-plan`/`re-verify:plan` prompts require a mechanical `test -f`/read check that `_plan.md` was actually authored — so a run reports `verified: true` over an unwritten rollup. None of the described fix was applied to this file.

structured_output.summary: The reported fix for #79 was never applied. `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` is still in its exact pre-fix state: `VERIFY_SCHEMA` (line 546) is `required: ['pass','planPath','gaps']` with no `planWritten`; the `verify-plan` (~1119-1137) and `re-verify:plan` (~1219-1221) prompts carry no rollup postcondition ("ROLLUP POSTCONDITION", `test -f ${PLAN_PATH}`) — the string appears nowhere in the repo; and line 1241 is still `const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`. `grep -ri planwritten` over the whole tree matches only the spec document. The report's own line citations (`:1276-1277` for `verified`, `:1261` for `verdict = reVerdict`) don't exist — the real file is ~27 lines shorter, i.e. it never grew. I confirmed the behaviour directly with a temporary probe test using the harness's pre-existing `DigestPatch`: on a clean acyclic gap-free seed, patching the `verify-plan` digest to `pass:true, planWritten:false` yields `m.verified === true` (AC-001 demands false), and forcing the fix-pass path with `re-verify:plan` reporting `pass:true, planWritten:false` also yields `m.verified === true` (AC-003 demands false). The dispatched verify schema's `required` array has no `planWritten`. The defect is silent because the guarding tests were never added either: `vitest run test/plan-dag.test.ts` passes 21/21, not the 25/25 the report claims, and there is no `AC-PW` describe block, no `patch` parameter on `run()`, no `planWritten` in `digestFor`, and no #79 entry in CHANGELOG (it appears only as a cross-reference inside the #73 entry). The defect therefore lives where the issue said it did — the verify/rollup step of forge-plan-prds.js, which derives a filesystem fact (`_plan.md` was authored) from the agent's own unverified `pass` flag.

findings.claim: A passing command gate's real shell-out executes while the shared cross-worktree write lock is held; no pre-flight pass and no cache-hot confirm exist.
findings.rationale: I ran the probe directly (not via the harness's non-filtering pnpm command) and watched the gate script record the lock directory as PRESENT at shell-out time, with exactly one real execution and zero cache hits — the behaviour AC-001 forbids. This is direct observation of the fault, not inference from the source.

repro.command: node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts --reporter=verbose
repro.expected_when_met: Probe log "U": the one real execution happens before withWriteLock is entered, and the in-lock confirm is a verify-cache HIT with no second shell-out.
repro.observed: PASS-GATE probe log: "L" — one real gate execution, taken while <git-common-dir>/redkiln/.write.lock existed (advance landed on implement). A companion run I added recorded the lock dir as absent immediately before and after advance(), so the L is caused by advance()'s own withWriteLock acquisition, not a stale directory.

findings.claim: A FAILING command gate still enters withWriteLock: the lock directory is created and the gate shells out twice inside it before the advance is refused.
findings.rationale: Observed directly: the probe's failing-gate case logged two shell-outs, both with the write lock directory present. AC-002 requires the throw to happen before withWriteLock is ever entered and requires that no lock directory be created at all.

repro.command: node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts --reporter=verbose
repro.expected_when_met: Probe log "U" (or "UU"), thrown before any lock acquisition, with the .write.lock directory never created.
repro.observed: FAIL-GATE probe log: "LL" (two real runs — src/store/verify.ts:739 gives the heavy suite one retry — both inside the lock), then GateError "command gate failed (EC-003)". The lock directory was demonstrably created for a blocked advance.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test does not discriminate: applying the spec's prescribed pre-flight restructure verbatim to engine.ts:769-772 leaves its output byte-identical, so the hypothesis's "the defect is solely the lock scope in advance()" is falsified.
findings.rationale: I mutated the code toward the fixed shape (the spec's own snippet, minus the telemetry-only preflightOnly flag) and the discriminating test's observed behaviour did not change at all — it stayed red with the identical L/LL log. The cause is in the same file but not at the named lines: advanceUnlocked's dry-run path returns at engine.ts:1058, before the walk loop that evaluates the TARGET stage's ENTRY gate at engine.ts:1340, and the probe drives plan -> implement, an entry-gate transition (the spec's own flagship repro, 'advance --to implement --apply'). Independently, previewExitGate (engine.ts:455-500) converts a GateError into a failing preview rather than throwing, so the pre-flight could not throw before the lock in the exit-gate direction either. The spec's premise that the dry-run path 'evaluates every gate ... and throws on failure' is wrong in both directions, so a root cause scoped to lines 769-772 alone is not actionable as stated.

repro.command: Applied to src/process/engine.ts:769-772 --- export function advance(id, opts) { if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts); advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false }); return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts)); } --- then: node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts --reporter=verbose (patch reverted afterwards with git checkout)
repro.expected_when_met: With the restructure genuinely in place, the pre-flight pass shells out before the lock: PASS-GATE "U" and FAIL-GATE throwing with no lock directory ever created. A test that cannot tell the two code states apart discriminates nothing.
repro.observed: Identical to the unpatched run: PASS-GATE probe log "L", FAIL-GATE probe log "LL", both tests red. The pre-flight pass ran (pass-case duration rose 7.3s -> 38.3s) but never shelled out at all, because the dry run returns at engine.ts:1058 before the entry gate at 1340.

It supports the hypothesis's headline conclusion (the fix was never implemented) while correcting one of its evidentiary statements: the report does not 'describe changes that are not in the tree' — its TDD-evidence, commits, changes and gates sections are the empty scaffold, so it asserts nothing at all.

repro.expected_when_met: A rebuilt dist carrying the pre-flight restructure, one Unreleased/Fixed CHANGELOG entry, and a filled implementation report mapping tests to AC-001..AC-005.
repro.observed: dist/cli.js:14969 still reads `return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts));`; no Unreleased entry mentions the write lock; the implementation report contains only empty template tables; git status shows only the investigator's untracked probe file.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001..AC-005 is implemented. AC-001 and AC-002 are demonstrably unmet — I reproduced the gate shelling out inside the held write lock on a passing gate, and the lock being created and shelled out in twice on a blocked advance. AC-003/AC-004/AC-005 are only vacuously satisfied because the second pass they govern does not exist, so they cannot evidence anything.

Nothing outside the frozen boundary was touched, because nothing was touched at all: git status shows a clean tree apart from the investigator's own untracked probe file. My temporary engine.ts mutation was reverted with git checkout and my scratch test file deleted, leaving the tree as found.

No regression test exists for any AC (vitest: 'No test files found' for test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts), and the three nearest suites pass 53/53 with the fault present. The only probe is untracked and, per my mutation experiment, non-discriminating for the entry-gate transition it exercises: it produces identical output whether or not the prescribed restructure is applied.

Targeted suites (lock, engine-advance, gate-memo-and-artifacts) are green, but the merge gate `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` was never observed green — the only full run attempted was killed at 420s, and the suite is genuinely slow (index-build 53s, doctor 53s, store-write 69s). NF-002 is therefore unverified rather than violated.

The working tree contains no source change, so no regression can have been introduced. The risk that matters here is the opposite one — the defect is still live and uncovered — which is scored under ac-coverage and test-integrity, not here.

root_cause.summary: advance() in src/process/engine.ts (lines 769-772) still wraps the entire advanceUnlocked call — including the command gate's synchronous shell-out via evaluateGate/evaluateCommand — in withWriteLock, so the shared cross-worktree write lock is held for the whole duration of the gate's test suite. The specified pre-flight-outside-the-lock restructure and its preflightOnly option on AdvanceOptions were never added to the file.

hypothesis.summary: The RK-S0263 fix was never implemented — the implementation report describes changes that are not in the tree. src/process/engine.ts:769-772 still reads the exact pre-fix shape the spec quotes (dry-run early return, then withWriteLock wrapping the whole advanceUnlocked call), with every spec line-reference still resolving unshifted (advanceUnlocked at 774, emitInto at 1099, exit-gate evaluateGate at 1157). None of the claimed artefacts exist: preflightOnly appears nowhere outside spec.md prose; the four claimed helpers (headResolves, gateMemoUsable, isMemoizedVerifyGate, preflightStage) are absent from src/, test/ and dist/; test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist; CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased/Fixed has no entry for it; dist/cli.js:14969 still carries the pre-fix wrapping. git status was clean, so there is no partial uncommitted work either. I verified the behaviour rather than inferring it: I wrote a probe test that drives a story to plan under a verify --grain story gate whose affected_gate script records whether the shared write-lock directory exists at shell-out time. Passing gate produced log "L" (the real run happened while the lock was held); failing gate produced "LL" (two real runs, both inside the lock, so withWriteLock was entered for a blocked advance, violating AC-002). The stack trace confirms the chain advance (engine.ts:771) -> withWriteLock (lock.ts:335) -> withSyncLock (lock.ts:255) -> advanceUnlocked (engine.ts:1340) -> evaluateGate -> evaluateCommand. gates.ts, verify-cache.ts and lock.ts are correct as-is per the spec and need no change; the defect is solely the lock scope in advance().

digest.discriminating_test: test/zz-issue77-probe.test.ts (I authored, ran, and then removed it to keep the tree clean; recreate to reproduce). Invoke as `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/zz-issue77-probe.test.ts` — NOT `pnpm test -- ...`, which puts every filter into cac's `--` bucket and runs the full suite. Three cases, all scaffolding a real git repo + `redkiln init` + initiative/project/story, committing the scaffold, then: (1) SINGLE-STEP — write `_review.md` into the story's own dir, run `advance <id> --to g1 --commit`, assert `git show --stat --name-only --pretty=format: HEAD` CONTAINS `_review.md`; (2) BLOCKED WALK — same, but on a 3-stage `walkblock` process whose g2 carries `gate: { kind: command, run: "node -e \"process.exit(1)\"", blocking: true }`, run `advance <id> --to g2 --commit` (exits 1) and assert the cleared-hop commit CONTAINS `_review.md`; (3) BOUNDARY — a second story `sib` under the same project with `_stray.md` in ITS dir, advance the first story, assert the commit does NOT contain `_stray.md`, that `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` still does, and that the commit DOES contain the `.redkiln/telemetry/events` partition. Observed at HEAD: (1) and (2) FAIL ("expected '.bklg/foundation/cutover/root/spec.md…' to contain '_review.md'", file left `??`), (3) passes. Observed with a patch confined to src/cli/advance.ts (both staging sites prepend `locateItem(root, id)?.dir`), src/process/engine.ts untouched: all 3 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Case (3) passing identically in both worlds is what discriminates "too-narrow staging set in advance.ts" from "staging is repo-wide/over-broad" or "commit() mishandles pathspecs"; case (2) discriminates a one-site fix from the two-site defect; the engine-untouched control discriminates advance.ts as the origin from engine.ts as a co-cause.

root_cause.summary: `src/cli/advance.ts` builds the `--commit` staging pathspec set from the transition's own `writtenPaths` alone — `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at the applied-advance commit (~line 123) and `err.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` in the `BlockedWalkError` catch (~line 220) — so companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_review.md`, a `_discovery/` corpus) are never staged and stay untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. Both sites are the same defect and both must widen to include the item's directory; the promised broadening was never implemented anywhere in the tree (no `itemDir` in src/ or dist/, no CHANGELOG entry, tests still pre-fix).

digest.summary:
The described fix never landed: no `itemDir` exists anywhere in `src/` (nor in the `dist/` build, which still emits `writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` at cli.js:15762/15817), CHANGELOG.md has no #77 entry, `test/advance-git-commit.test.ts` still holds the pre-fix 6-test set, and the item's on-disk implementation-report.md is the unfilled template. The whole target suite is 6/6 green at HEAD, so nothing in-repo signals the fault — it is silent.

Correcting my previous pass on the reviewer's three substantive points: (a) I replaced the inert name-filter with an executable probe run via `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` (never `pnpm test --`, which routes filters into cac's `--` bucket and sweeps the whole suite); at HEAD it is 2 failed / 1 passed, under the patch 3 passed — an exit-status difference, not a match artifact. (b) I exercised the blocked-walk path with a purpose-built 3-stage `walkblock` process (g1 clean, g2 blocking command gate): at HEAD the gate-blocked `advance --to g2 --commit` commits spec.md/story.md/telemetry and leaves `?? .bklg/foundation/cutover/root/_review.md`, confirming the `BlockedWalkError` catch at advance.ts:220 is a second, independent instance of the same defect. (c) I narrowed the file set by patching `src/cli/advance.ts` ALONE (deriving the dir via `locateItem(root, id)?.dir`, both staging sites) with `src/process/engine.ts` byte-identical to HEAD: `tsc --noEmit` clean and all three probes green. The engine faithfully reports what the transition wrote and the spec explicitly leaves `writtenPaths`' meaning unchanged, so `AdvanceResult.itemDir` is the chosen fix shape, not the origin of the wrong behaviour — engine.ts is dropped from the root cause.

Boundary and regression evidence: a sibling story's `_stray.md` (planted in that item's own directory, which no existing test does) stays out of the commit and remains untracked in both worlds; the telemetry partition stays in the commit in both worlds (AC-003 additive holds); under the patch the existing suite is 5 passed / 1 failed with the single failure being the "narrow staging" test the spec mandates inverting, and the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression (AC-004) stays green. `src/git/index.ts`'s `commit()` is exonerated — its `git add -- <dir>` recursed into the item directory correctly and unmodified. The scratch patch and probe file were reverted; `git status --porcelain` is empty.

root_cause.summary: The project-only frontmatter field `terminal` (DoD-owner role) is parsed into the store but never carried into the derived index: `SCHEMA`'s `items` table in src/index/build.ts has no `dod_owner` column and `insertItems` binds no parameter for `data.terminal`, so src/index/queries.ts's `items()`/`ItemProjection` can only expose the pack-derived lifecycle `terminal` and a DoD-owner project is indistinguishable from a non-owner in `status --json`. The reported `dod_owner`/`dodOwner` addition is absent from the tree entirely (no column, no field, no tests, no CHANGELOG entry), so the original defect still sits at its origin in these two files.

digest.summary: I read src/index/build.ts (SCHEMA + insertItems) and src/index/queries.ts (ItemProjection + items()) and found no `dod_owner` column and no `dodOwner` field anywhere in src/ or test/. I then produced my own evidence with two throwaway probe specs (since removed, tree left clean): loadStore reports `terminal: true` for the RK-P0001 project fixture, but the built SQLite `items` table has no `dod_owner` column and `items()` returns byte-identical projections for a `terminal: true` owner and a `terminal: false` non-owner — both `terminal: false`, no `dodOwner` key. `vitest -t \"dod_owner\"` matches zero tests and CHANGELOG has no #82 entry, so the reported implementation never landed; the wrong behaviour originates in the index write path (build.ts) and the projection it feeds (queries.ts), not in src/cli/status.ts, which merely prints the projection, nor in src/schema/item.ts / src/store/verify.ts, which handle the frontmatter field correctly.

root_cause.summary: The project-only frontmatter field `terminal` (DoD-owner role) is parsed into the store but never carried into the derived index: `SCHEMA`'s `items` table in src/index/build.ts has no `dod_owner` column and `insertItems` binds no parameter for `data.terminal`, so src/index/queries.ts's `items()`/`ItemProjection` can only expose the pack-derived lifecycle `terminal` and a DoD-owner project is indistinguishable from a non-owner in `status --json`. hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/plan-dag.test.ts — a DigestPatch case on a clean acyclic seed rewriting the `verify-plan` digest to `{pass: true, planWritten: false}` (and a second forcing the fix pass so `re-verify:plan` reports `{pass: true, planWritten: false}`), asserting `m.verified === false`. I ran exactly this as a scratch file (test/zz-probe-issue79.test.ts, since deleted) and observed `verified: true` in both cases.

root_cause.summary: workflows/forge-plan-prds.js still computes the manifest's `verified` from the verify agent's self-reported `pass` alone (`const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`, line 1241), and neither VERIFY_SCHEMA (line 546, no `planWritten` field) nor the `verify-plan`/`re-verify:plan` prompts require a mechanical `test -f`/read check that `_plan.md` was actually authored — so a run reports `verified: true` over an unwritten rollup. None of the described fix was applied to this file.

hypothesis.summary: The reported fix for #79 was never applied. `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` is still in its exact pre-fix state: `VERIFY_SCHEMA` (line 546) is `required: ['pass','planPath','gaps']` with no `planWritten`; the `verify-plan` (~1119-1137) and `re-verify:plan` (~1219-1221) prompts carry no rollup postcondition ("ROLLUP POSTCONDITION", `test -f ${PLAN_PATH}`) — the string appears nowhere in the repo; and line 1241 is still `const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0;`. `grep -ri planwritten` over the whole tree matches only the spec document. The report's own line citations (`:1276-1277` for `verified`, `:1261` for `verdict = reVerdict`) don't exist — the real file is ~27 lines shorter, i.e. it never grew. I confirmed the behaviour directly with a temporary probe test using the harness's pre-existing `DigestPatch`: on a clean acyclic gap-free seed, patching the `verify-plan` digest to `pass:true, planWritten:false` yields `m.verified === true` (AC-001 demands false), and forcing the fix-pass path with `re-verify:plan` reporting `pass:true, planWritten:false` also yields `m.verified === true` (AC-003 demands false). The dispatched verify schema's `required` array has no `planWritten`. The defect is silent because the guarding tests were never added either: `vitest run test/plan-dag.test.ts` passes 21/21, not the 25/25 the report claims, and there is no `AC-PW` describe block, no `patch` parameter on `run()`, no `planWritten` in `digestFor`, and no #79 entry in CHANGELOG (it appears only as a cross-reference inside the #73 entry). The defect therefore lives where the issue said it did — the verify/rollup step of forge-plan-prds.js, which derives a filesystem fact (`_plan.md` was authored) from the agent's own unverified `pass` flag.

The implementation report describes a `releaseLock` helper, `test/lock.test.ts` and a CHANGELOG entry that do not exist in the tree.

digest.summary: Read src/store/lock.ts end to end: both release sites are the unmodified single-attempt `try { rmdirSync(path) } catch {}` in `finally`; grep found no releaseLock/RELEASE_ATTEMPTS/RELEASE_RETRY_MS and no warning emission anywhere. The report's cited artifacts are absent (no test/lock.test.ts; test/ids.test.ts is 380 lines with no AC-003 block; CHANGELOG has no #66 entry). Prior waves' fixes (dodOwner for #82) ARE present in src/, so this is not a stale checkout — only this change is missing. I then reproduced all three behavioral ACs against HEAD with scratch vitest files (since deleted; tree clean): mocked rmdirSync made exactly one attempt and left the lock directory behind, emitted zero stderr warnings, and a fully sequential second withIdLock after one injected transient EBUSY rejected with LockTimeoutError (EC-001) — the issue's exact shape. The defect therefore still lives at its origin, the release finally blocks in src/store/lock.ts (plus the stale doc comment in src/store/ids.ts for AC-005).

findings.claim: Neither the hypothesis nor the spec's frozen boundary accounts for the fixture edits that AC-001..AC-004 verification actually requires, so the declared boundary is unsatisfiable as written.
findings.rationale: I can evidence the premise (no committed fixture carries `terminal:`, and the sibling reference fix edits two project.md files that the frozen-boundary table in spec.md does not list), but this is a forward-looking concern about the implementation the hypothesis feeds, not a demonstrated defect in the root-cause claim itself. Reporting it as advisory rather than inflating it.

repro.command: diff -rq ../../e3-silent-issue-82-.../test ../../e3-clean-issue-82-.../test
repro.expected_when_met: Either the boundary table names the fixture files, or AC-001..AC-004 are verifiable with fixtures created inside test/queries-status.test.ts itself, with no edit outside the frozen list.
repro.observed: The reference fix additionally modifies test/fixtures/status/.bklg/client-foundation/{api-platform,web-cutover}/project.md (adding `terminal: false` / `terminal: true`) — paths absent from the spec's "Frozen PR boundary" table, which lists only src/index/build.ts, src/index/queries.ts, test/index-build.test.ts, test/queries-status.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md.

rubric.rationale: The root cause names exactly the two files the reference fix touches, and I confirmed by construction that editing only src/index/build.ts and src/index/queries.ts makes items() report dodOwner true/false — so it is an origin claim (the index write path plus the projection type), not a symptom claim, and it is narrow enough to act on. status.ts is correctly exculpated (buildReport passes q.items() through generically, no hardcoded field list), as are schema/item.ts and store/verify.ts (isTerminalProject reads raw frontmatter). Marked down because the hypothesis offers no evidence touching AC-003 (null for non-project types) or AC-005 (terminal semantics unchanged), and its one stated store observation does not reproduce on the committed tree.

Both named files sit inside the spec's frozen PR boundary, and the investigator's claim that the tree was left clean checks out: git status was empty when I arrived and empty again after I restored my own experiment (git checkout -- src/index/build.ts src/index/queries.ts; rm test/zz-adversarial-probe.test.ts). No stray dod_owner/dodOwner artifacts anywhere in src/ or test/.

The nominated discriminating test matches zero of 22 tests and passes vacuously; applying the real fix leaves its output byte-identical, so it separates nothing. The supporting evidence was two throwaway probes that were deleted, and the one observation quoted from them (loadStore reporting terminal: true for RK-P0001) is false of the committed fixture, which has no terminal key. The underlying conclusion survives only because I re-derived it with my own probe and an explicit fixture mutation.

The gate as executed (pnpm test -- --run test/index-build.test.ts -t dod_owner) failed to scope to the file, ran the full suite, and was killed at 420s with no verdict. The correctly scoped form I ran exits 0 while the defect is fully present, so no gate in this repository currently distinguishes the fixed from the unfixed state; no test pins dodOwner at any level.

Nothing was changed in the tree, and the identified fix path is purely additive: a nullable column plus one bound parameter, with INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION = shortDigest(SCHEMA) (build.ts:491) guaranteeing stale on-disk caches are invalidated automatically — I read that derivation rather than taking it on assertion. Grepping workflows/ and commands/ found no consumer that reads items[].terminal from status --json expecting the DoD-owner role (implement.md takes terminal as an operator-supplied argument), so the additive fix strands no downstream reader.

findings.claim: The nominated discriminating test cannot discriminate: it produces byte-identical output and exit 0 both on the faulty tree and after the claimed root cause is fully fixed.
findings.rationale: I did not merely reason about the filter — I changed the behaviour under test (copied the reference implementation of the two named files from the sibling e3-clean-issue-82 fixture, so `dod_owner`/`dodOwner` genuinely exist and work) and re-ran the exact nominated command. It stayed green and its output diffed clean against the pre-fix run. A command whose result is invariant across the fix/no-fix boundary is by definition not a discriminator, so `mutation-survived` is the honest class rather than `advisory`.

repro.expected_when_met: A genuine discriminator would differ across that boundary: red (a failing assertion naming dodOwner) before the fix in build.ts/queries.ts, green after it — e.g. the AC-001 test the spec prescribes in test/queries-status.test.ts asserting `items().find(i => i.id === 'RK-P0001').dodOwner === true`.
repro.observed: Both runs: "Test Files 1 skipped (1) / Tests 22 skipped (22)", VITEST-EXIT=0. The diff of the two runs is empty (IDENTICAL OUTPUT). A separate probe confirmed the world really had changed under the fix: `HAS dod_owner = true`, `dodOwner: true` for RK-P0001 and `dodOwner: false` for RK-P0002.

findings.claim: The hypothesis states the named command "fails today"; the command actually passes with exit 0 on the unmodified faulty tree.
findings.rationale: I ran the scoped command on the tree as committed and captured the process exit code directly rather than through a pipe. vitest 2.1.9 treats a `-t` filter matching nothing inside an included file as 22 skipped tests, not an error, so the stated expectation ("it fails today because the key does not exist") is contradicted by observation. This is a claim about what I ran and watched, so `reproduced`.

findings.claim: The evidence cited for the hypothesis ("loadStore reports `terminal: true` for the RK-P0001 project fixture") does not reproduce against the repository as committed; that fixture carries no `terminal` key at all.

Classifying as `reproduced` because I ran the stated observation and watched it come out differently.

You are given their hypothesis and the result of the discriminating test they named. You have the repository. Check the claim yourself rather than reasoning about it.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:
- it names a symptom, not the origin: the file where the wrong value is PRINTED rather than where it is computed
- it names the right area but the wrong file, or a set so broad it is not actionable
- the discriminating test does not in fact discriminate: it would pass or fail the same way either way
- the evidence offered does not support the claim, even though the claim may happen to be true

Classify every finding by the evidence you actually have. `reproduced` means you ran something and watched it behave as you describe. `mutation-survived` means you changed a behaviour and the suite stayed green. `narrowed-pin` means a test pins a narrower claim than the requirement behind it. `advisory` is anything you could not evidence at that bar — use it honestly rather than inflating a hunch.

You return no verdict. It is computed from your findings.","tools":["Read","Bash","StructuredOutput"],"model":"opus","effort":"xhigh"}}

ADDRESSING THE REVIEWER, POINT BY POINT.

(1) Test-integrity — I replaced the absent artifact with an IN-TREE, zero-pollution discriminator and ran it: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "narrow staging"` → "1 passed | 5 skipped". That test asserts the PRE-fix behaviour, so its passing is direct evidence the fix is absent; under a conforming fix it is the single failure in the file. No `pnpm test --` involved (the reviewer is right that pnpm routes filters into cac's `--` bucket and sweeps the suite; I never used that shape this pass).
