I ran exactly these as a throwaway spec against this checkout: 3 of 4 fail today and all pass once step 9 carries the sub-step.

root_cause.summary: `commands/plan.md` step 9 instructs the orchestrator to run `redkiln advance <STORY-ID> --to spec --apply` on a freshly-scaffolded standard-tier story without first authoring the rendered `discover.md` and ticking its four `## Gate: Discover` boxes, so the hard-blocking `gates/discover` checklist gate on the `story` pack's `discover` stage always fails the advance. The claimed authoring/ticking sub-step (and its EC-001 stale-template fallback) was never added to the file.

digest.summary: The reported fix for #81 is not present in the tree. `commands/plan.md` step 9 still goes straight from `redkiln new story ...` to `redkiln advance <STORY-ID> --to spec --apply` for a standard-tier story, with no sub-step that authors the rendered `discover.md` (Signal Ledger / Questions / Decision) and ticks the four `## Gate: Discover` boxes, and no EC-001 stale-template fallback. Grep of `commands/plan.md` finds no `gates/discover`, `tick`, `Signal Ledger`, or `adopt --templates` anywhere inside step 9 (lines 276-292) — only step 5's unrelated `gates/intake` text at line 202. I reproduced the bug live against this checkout's own CLI: init → new initiative → new project → `new story` (standard `story` pack) → `redkiln advance <ID> --to spec --apply` exits 1 with `checklist gate 'gates/discover' failed: 4 required item(s) not ticked`, and the freshly rendered `discover.md` has all four boxes empty. That confirms the engine, `processes/story.yaml`'s `discover` gate, and `templates/gates/discover.md` are all behaving as designed (AC-003 holds; `test/e2e-acceptance.test.ts`'s "a checklist gate with an unchecked item blocks discover -> spec" passes) — the wrong behaviour originates purely in the instruction text of step 9, which directs an advance across a gate it never satisfies. It is silent because the AC-001/AC-002 guard assertions the report claims to have added to `test/plan-contract.test.ts` are also absent (file ends at line 211, 33/33 green), and `CHANGELOG.md` has no #81 entry. Narrowest fix: restore the discover-authoring + checklist-ticking sub-step in `commands/plan.md` step 9, standard-tier only (the `story-lite` `intake → spec` branch is correctly untouched).

I reproduced the bug live against this checkout's own CLI: init → new initiative → new project → `new story` (standard `story` pack) → `redkiln advance <ID> --to spec --apply` exits 1 with `checklist gate 'gates/discover' failed: 4 required item(s) not ticked`, and the freshly rendered `discover.md` has all four boxes empty. findings.claim: The shared cross-worktree write lock is held for the entire duration of the command gate's execution, so the gate never runs unlocked.
findings.rationale: I wrote and ran a probe test that declares verify.affected_gate as a script recording whether <root>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock exists at the instant it runs, and drove a real `advance --apply` across the `implement` command gate on a git-identified tree. I observed the recorded state directly rather than inferring it from reading advance().

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts  (temporary probe: seeds a story to `plan`, sets verify.affected_gate to a node script appending "locked"/"unlocked" based on existsSync(<work>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock), then `advance <id> --apply`)
repro.expected_when_met: log= ["unlocked"] — the gate's real execution happens outside withWriteLock, with the in-lock confirm being a verify-cache hit.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE code= 0 log= ["locked"] — the gate executed exactly once and the write-lock directory existed while it ran.

findings.claim: A failing command gate still enters withWriteLock: the lock directory is created and held while the gate runs (twice), before the GateError propagates.
findings.rationale: Same probe, gate script exiting 1. The recorded log shows the lock directory present at both gate invocations, which is direct observation that withWriteLock was entered before the refusal, not a reading of the code.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts (failing-gate case: probe script exits 1)
repro.expected_when_met: log empty or all "unlocked", and the lock directory never created for a blocked advance.
repro.observed: FAILING-GATE code= 1 log= ["locked","locked"] — lock dir present for the run and the flake-tolerance re-run.

findings.claim: The discriminating test named for this root cause does not discriminate: it fails identically whether or not the hypothesised fix is present, because the file does not exist.
findings.rationale: I ran the exact named command in two states — the pristine tree, and a tree with the hypothesised pre-flight restructure applied to advance(). Both produced exit 1 with "No test files found". The signal is a missing-file error, carrying zero information about lock scope.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts   # run once on HEAD, once with `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` inserted before withWriteLock in src/process/engine.ts
repro.expected_when_met: A discriminating test exists and its pass/fail flips with the presence of the fix — failing (asserting ["unlocked"] but observing ["locked"]) on HEAD and passing once the gate runs outside the lock.
repro.observed: Both runs: "No test files found, exiting with code 1"; exit=1. Identical output in the faulty and the purportedly-fixed state.

findings.claim: The causal mechanism named — that the missing piece is an unlocked pre-flight pass plus a `preflightOnly` field on AdvanceOptions — is falsified: applying exactly that change leaves the fault bit-for-bit unchanged.
findings.rationale: I mutated src/process/engine.ts to the spec's literal prescription and re-ran the probe: identical results. I then instrumented every evaluateGate call site and the dry-run early return to see why. The trace shows the pre-flight returns at engine.ts:1071 without evaluating any gate, and the command gate is evaluated only after lock-enter, as the TARGET stage's entry gate at engine.ts:1354 inside walkToTarget — a path the dry-run/pre-flight branch never reaches. This is observation of control flow, not a reading.

repro.command: Insert `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` before `return withWriteLock(...)` in src/process/engine.ts:769-772, add probeTrace() markers at engine.ts:1071 (dry-run return), :1171 (exit gate), :1354 (entry gate) and in previewExitGate, then `npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts`
repro.expected_when_met: If the named missing change were the cause, the same mutation would yield log= ["unlocked"] and, for the failing gate, a throw from the pre-flight with no lock-enter in the trace.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE log= ["locked"] (unchanged); FAILING-GATE log= ["locked","locked"] (unchanged). trace= ... preflight-enter | dryrun-return:current=plan:gate=none | preflight-ok | lock-enter | entry-gate-eval:implement:command — the pre-flight evaluated no gate and did not throw even for the failing gate.

findings.claim: The prescribed pre-flight restructure is not merely insufficient but regressive: it silently defeats the gate memo's bypass flags, so `--fresh` and REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 no longer force a real in-lock run.
findings.rationale: I ran the full suite with the prescribed mutation applied and watched two pre-existing AC-MEMO-BYPASS assertions turn red for exactly this reason — the unlocked pre-flight repopulates the memo, so the locked confirm reuses it. This is the AC-005 hazard class (a stale pre-flight pass standing in for a real in-lock check) materialising in the repo's own existing coverage.

repro.command: Apply the pre-flight mutation to src/process/engine.ts:769-772, then `npx vitest run`
repro.expected_when_met: A correct pre-flight/confirm split threads the bypass flags so `--fresh` still forces a real run inside the lock; the suite stays at 1915 passed.
repro.observed: Test Files 1 failed | 93 passed; Tests 2 failed | 1913 passed. FAIL AC-MEMO-BYPASS: --fresh forces a real run — expected 'redkiln: reusing the verified \'story…' not to match /reusing the verified/; FAIL AC-MEMO-BYPASS: REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 disables the memo — expected 3 to be 2.

findings.claim: No test in the suite pins single gate_result emission per transition, and the `preflightOnly` field the root cause names as missing is not load-bearing for that hazard — emitGateResult already returns early on commit !== true.
findings.rationale: I added a second full advanceUnlocked pass with NO telemetry suppression whatsoever — the precise mutation AC-003 exists to catch — and the entire telemetry corpus (gate-telemetry, telemetry-order, telemetry-emit, migration-telemetry) stayed green; only the two unrelated memo-bypass tests broke. The guard at engine.ts:1124 (`if (opts.commit !== true) return;`) explains why no double-emit occurs, which means the absence of `preflightOnly` cannot be part of the cause of the lock-scope fault.

repro.command: Apply `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` before withWriteLock with no telemetry suppression, then `npx vitest run`
repro.expected_when_met: A test asserting exactly one gate_result per gate per --apply transition would either fail under an unsuppressed double pass, or the requirement would be recognised as already satisfied by the existing commit guard rather than needing a new flag.
repro.observed: 1913 passed; zero telemetry-related failures. src/process/engine.ts:1124 shows emitGateResult already short-circuits when opts.commit !== true.

findings.claim: No regression test exists for any acceptance criterion of this story; the merge gate is green vacuously because the product code is untouched.
findings.rationale: I ran the full suite on the pristine tree and it passes completely, while the probe I wrote demonstrates AC-001 and AC-002 are unmet. Green gates therefore carry no signal about this story. The claimed test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts is absent, implementation-report.md is an unfilled template, and CHANGELOG.md has no Unreleased entry for the write lock.

repro.command: npx vitest run ; git status --short ; git diff --stat HEAD ; grep -in 'write lock\|pre-flight' CHANGELOG.md
repro.expected_when_met: At least one test covering advance's lock behaviour exists and fails on HEAD; CHANGELOG carries one Unreleased entry; the implementation report maps tests to ACs.
repro.observed: Test Files 94 passed (94), Tests 1915 passed (1915). Working tree clean, empty diff vs HEAD (single commit 'chore(...): advance to implement'). No CHANGELOG entry. implementation-report.md TDD-evidence and Commits tables are empty template rows.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001..AC-005 are implemented or covered. I reproduced AC-001 and AC-002 as actively violated (gate runs with the write lock held: ["locked"] and ["locked","locked"]). AC-003/AC-004/AC-005 have no test at all, and the named regression file test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist. The product code at src/process/engine.ts:769-772 is unchanged from the pre-fix snippet the spec quotes.

The frozen boundary permits src/process/engine.ts, test/, and CHANGELOG.md. `git diff --stat HEAD` is empty and `git status --short` is clean at the single 'advance to implement' commit, so nothing outside the boundary was touched — trivially respected, because nothing was touched at all. gates.ts, verify-cache.ts and lock.ts are unmodified, which the spec requires.

The discriminating test named for this root cause is non-discriminating: I ran `npx vitest run test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` on HEAD and on a tree with the hypothesised fix applied, and both produced 'No test files found, exiting with code 1'. The signal is a missing-file error carrying no information about lock scope. No test anywhere in the 94-file suite exercises write-lock hold time, and I confirmed by mutation that a second unsuppressed advanceUnlocked pass leaves the telemetry corpus entirely green.

The merge gate genuinely passes — 94 files, 1915 tests green on the untouched tree, reproduced by me. But the greenness is vacuous: it is green because no code changed, and my probe shows the behaviour the story exists to fix is still broken underneath it. Green here actively masks the defect rather than evidencing it.

Nothing shipped, so the delivered regression risk is nil. But the fix direction the root cause prescribes is demonstrably regressive: applying it verbatim turned two pre-existing AC-MEMO-BYPASS tests red (--fresh and REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 stop forcing a real in-lock run because the unlocked pre-flight repopulates the memo), and it does not move the entry-gate shell-out out of the lock at all. Acting on this root cause as written would ship a regression without fixing the fault.

findings.claim: The shared cross-worktree write lock is held for the entire duration of the command gate's execution, so the gate never runs unlocked.
findings.rationale: I wrote and ran a probe test that declares verify.affected_gate as a script recording whether <root>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock exists at the instant it runs, and drove a real `advance --apply` across the `implement` command gate on a git-identified tree. I observed the recorded state directly rather than inferring it from reading advance().

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts  (temporary probe: seeds a story to `plan`, sets verify.affected_gate to a node script appending "locked"/"unlocked" based on existsSync(<work>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock), then `advance <id> --apply`)
repro.expected_when_met: log= ["unlocked"] — the gate's real execution happens outside withWriteLock, with the in-lock confirm being a verify-cache hit.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE code= 0 log= ["locked"] — the gate executed exactly once and the write-lock directory existed while it ran.

findings.claim: A failing command gate still enters withWriteLock: the lock directory is created and held while the gate runs (twice), before the GateError propagates.

repro.observed: FAILING-GATE code= 1 log= ["locked","locked"] — lock dir present for the run and the flake-tolerance re-run.

findings.claim: The discriminating test named for this root cause does not discriminate: it fails identically whether or not the hypothesised fix is present, because the file does not exist.
findings.rationale: I ran the exact named command in two states — the pristine tree, and a tree with the hypothesised pre-flight restructure applied to advance(). Both produced exit 1 with "No test files found". The signal is a missing-file error, carrying zero information about lock scope.

repro.expected_when_met: A discriminating test exists and its pass/fail flips with the presence of the fix — failing (asserting ["unlocked"] but observing ["locked"]) on HEAD and passing once the gate runs outside the lock.
repro.observed: Both runs: "No test files found, exiting with code 1"; exit=1. Identical output in the faulty and the purportedly-fixed state.

findings.claim: The causal mechanism named — that the missing piece is an unlocked pre-flight pass plus a `preflightOnly` field on AdvanceOptions — is falsified: applying exactly that change leaves the fault bit-for-bit unchanged.
findings.rationale: I mutated src/process/engine.ts to the spec's literal prescription and re-ran the probe: identical results. I then instrumented every evaluateGate call site and the dry-run early return to see why. The trace shows the pre-flight returns at engine.ts:1071 without evaluating any gate, and the command gate is evaluated only after lock-enter, as the TARGET stage's entry gate at engine.ts:1354 inside walkToTarget — a path the dry-run/pre-flight branch never reaches. This is observation of control flow, not a reading.

repro.command: Insert `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` before `return withWriteLock(...)` in src/process/engine.ts:769-772, add probeTrace() markers at engine.ts:1071 (dry-run return), :1171 (exit gate), :1354 (entry gate) and in previewExitGate, then `npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts`
repro.expected_when_met: If the named missing change were the cause, the same mutation would yield log= ["unlocked"] and, for the failing gate, a throw from the pre-flight with no lock-enter in the trace.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE log= ["locked"] (unchanged); FAILING-GATE log= ["locked","locked"] (unchanged). trace= ... preflight-enter | dryrun-return:current=plan:gate=none | preflight-ok | lock-enter | entry-gate-eval:implement:command — the pre-flight evaluated no gate and did not throw even for the failing gate.

findings.claim: The shared cross-worktree write lock is held for the entire duration of the command gate's execution, so the gate never runs unlocked.
findings.rationale: I wrote and ran a probe test that declares verify.affected_gate as a script recording whether <root>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock exists at the instant it runs, and drove a real `advance --apply` across the `implement` command gate on a git-identified tree. I observed the recorded state directly rather than inferring it from reading advance().

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts  (temporary probe: seeds a story to `plan`, sets verify.affected_gate to a node script appending "locked"/"unlocked" based on existsSync(<work>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock), then `advance <id> --apply`)
repro.expected_when_met: log= ["unlocked"] — the gate's real execution happens outside withWriteLock, with the in-lock confirm being a verify-cache hit.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE code= 0 log= ["locked"] — the gate executed exactly once and the write-lock directory existed while it ran.

findings.claim: A failing command gate still enters withWriteLock: the lock directory is created and held while the gate runs (twice), before the GateError propagates.
findings.rationale: Same probe, gate script exiting 1. The recorded log shows the lock directory present at both gate invocations, which is direct observation that withWriteLock was entered before the refusal, not a reading of the code.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts (failing-gate case: probe script exits 1)
repro.expected_when_met: log empty or all "unlocked", and the lock directory never created for a blocked advance.
repro.observed: FAILING-GATE code= 1 log= ["locked","locked"] — lock dir present for the run and the flake-tolerance re-run.

findings.claim: The discriminating test named for this root cause does not discriminate: it fails identically whether or not the hypothesised fix is present, because the file does not exist.
findings.rationale: I ran the exact named command in two states — the pristine tree, and a tree with the hypothesised pre-flight restructure applied to advance(). Both produced exit 1 with "No test files found". The signal is a missing-file error, carrying zero information about lock scope.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts   # run once on HEAD, once with `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` inserted before withWriteLock in src/process/engine.ts
repro.expected_when_met: A discriminating test exists and its pass/fail flips with the presence of the fix — failing (asserting ["unlocked"] but observing ["locked"]) on HEAD and passing once the gate runs outside the lock.
repro.observed: Both runs: "No test files found, exiting with code 1"; exit=1. Identical output in the faulty and the purportedly-fixed state.

findings.claim: The causal mechanism named — that the missing piece is an unlocked pre-flight pass plus a `preflightOnly` field on AdvanceOptions — is falsified: applying exactly that change leaves the fault bit-for-bit unchanged.
findings.rationale: I mutated src/process/engine.ts to the spec's literal prescription and re-ran the probe: identical results. I then instrumented every evaluateGate call site and the dry-run early return to see why. The trace shows the pre-flight returns at engine.ts:1071 without evaluating any gate, and the command gate is evaluated only after lock-enter, as the TARGET stage's entry gate at engine.ts:1354 inside walkToTarget — a path the dry-run/pre-flight branch never reaches. This is observation of control flow, not a reading.

repro.command: Insert `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` before `return withWriteLock(...)` in src/process/engine.ts:769-772, add probeTrace() markers at engine.ts:1071 (dry-run return), :1171 (exit gate), :1354 (entry gate) and in previewExitGate, then `npx vitest run test/zz-probe-lock-scope.test.ts`
repro.expected_when_met: If the named missing change were the cause, the same mutation would yield log= ["unlocked"] and, for the failing gate, a throw from the pre-flight with no lock-enter in the trace.
repro.observed: PASSING-GATE log= ["locked"] (unchanged); FAILING-GATE log= ["locked","locked"] (unchanged). trace= ... preflight-enter | dryrun-return:current=plan:gate=none | preflight-ok | lock-enter | entry-gate-eval:implement:command — the pre-flight evaluated no gate and did not throw even for the failing gate.

findings.claim: The prescribed pre-flight restructure is not merely insufficient but regressive: it silently defeats the gate memo's bypass flags, so `--fresh` and REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 no longer force a real in-lock run.
findings.rationale: I ran the full suite with the prescribed mutation applied and watched two pre-existing AC-MEMO-BYPASS assertions turn red for exactly this reason — the unlocked pre-flight repopulates the memo, so the locked confirm reuses it. This is the AC-005 hazard class (a stale pre-flight pass standing in for a real in-lock check) materialising in the repo's own existing coverage.

repro.command: Apply the pre-flight mutation to src/process/engine.ts:769-772, then `npx vitest run`
repro.expected_when_met: A correct pre-flight/confirm split threads the bypass flags so `--fresh` still forces a real run inside the lock; the suite stays at 1915 passed.
repro.observed: Test Files 1 failed | 93 passed; Tests 2 failed | 1913 passed. FAIL AC-MEMO-BYPASS: --fresh forces a real run — expected 'redkiln: reusing the verified \'story…' not to match /reusing the verified/; FAIL AC-MEMO-BYPASS: REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 disables the memo — expected 3 to be 2.

findings.claim: No test in the suite pins single gate_result emission per transition, and the `preflightOnly` field the root cause names as missing is not load-bearing for that hazard — emitGateResult already returns early on commit !== true.
findings.rationale: I added a second full advanceUnlocked pass with NO telemetry suppression whatsoever — the precise mutation AC-003 exists to catch — and the entire telemetry corpus (gate-telemetry, telemetry-order, telemetry-emit, migration-telemetry) stayed green; only the two unrelated memo-bypass tests broke. The guard at engine.ts:1124 (`if (opts.commit !== true) return;`) explains why no double-emit occurs, which means the absence of `preflightOnly` cannot be part of the cause of the lock-scope fault.

repro.command: Apply `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false });` before withWriteLock with no telemetry suppression, then `npx vitest run`
repro.expected_when_met: A test asserting exactly one gate_result per gate per --apply transition would either fail under an unsuppressed double pass, or the requirement would be recognised as already satisfied by the existing commit guard rather than needing a new flag.
repro.observed: 1913 passed; zero telemetry-related failures. src/process/engine.ts:1124 shows emitGateResult already short-circuits when opts.commit !== true.

findings.claim: No regression test exists for any acceptance criterion of this story; the merge gate is green vacuously because the product code is untouched.
findings.rationale: I ran the full suite on the pristine tree and it passes completely, while the probe I wrote demonstrates AC-001 and AC-002 are unmet. Green gates therefore carry no signal about this story. The claimed test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts is absent, implementation-report.md is an unfilled template, and CHANGELOG.md has no Unreleased entry for the write lock.

repro.command: npx vitest run ; git status --short ; git diff --stat HEAD ; grep -in 'write lock\|pre-flight' CHANGELOG.md
repro.expected_when_met: At least one test covering advance's lock behaviour exists and fails on HEAD; CHANGELOG carries one Unreleased entry; the implementation report maps tests to ACs.
repro.observed: Test Files 94 passed (94), Tests 1915 passed (1915). Working tree clean, empty diff vs HEAD (single commit 'chore(...): advance to implement'). No CHANGELOG entry. implementation-report.md TDD-evidence and Commits tables are empty template rows.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001..AC-005 are implemented or covered. I reproduced AC-001 and AC-002 as actively violated (gate runs with the write lock held: ["locked"] and ["locked","locked"]). AC-003/AC-004/AC-005 have no test at all, and the named regression file test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist. The product code at src/process/engine.ts:769-772 is unchanged from the pre-fix snippet the spec quotes.

The frozen boundary permits src/process/engine.ts, test/, and CHANGELOG.md. `git diff --stat HEAD` is empty and `git status --short` is clean at the single 'advance to implement' commit, so nothing outside the boundary was touched — trivially respected, because nothing was touched at all. gates.ts, verify-cache.ts and lock.ts are unmodified, which the spec requires.

The discriminating test named for this root cause is non-discriminating: I ran `npx vitest run test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` on HEAD and on a tree with the hypothesised fix applied, and both produced 'No test files found, exiting with code 1'. The signal is a missing-file error carrying no information about lock scope. No test anywhere in the 94-file suite exercises write-lock hold time, and I confirmed by mutation that a second unsuppressed advanceUnlocked pass leaves the telemetry corpus entirely green.

The merge gate genuinely passes — 94 files, 1915 tests green on the untouched tree, reproduced by me. But the greenness is vacuous: it is green because no code changed, and my probe shows the behaviour the story exists to fix is still broken underneath it. Green here actively masks the defect rather than evidencing it.

Nothing shipped, so the delivered regression risk is nil. But the fix direction the root cause prescribes is demonstrably regressive: applying it verbatim turned two pre-existing AC-MEMO-BYPASS tests red (--fresh and REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1 stop forcing a real in-lock run because the unlocked pre-flight repopulates the memo), and it does not move the entry-gate shell-out out of the lock at all. Acting on this root cause as written would ship a regression without fixing the fault.

hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts (missing) — equivalently: a vitest that seeds a story to `plan` on the bundled `story` pack, sets `verify.affected_gate` to a script appending "locked"/"unlocked" based on `existsSync(<root>/.git/redkiln/.write.lock)`, runs `advance <id> --apply`, and asserts the log is `["unlocked"]` (AC-001) and, for a failing gate, that the lock dir is never created (AC-002). I ran exactly this: it yields `["locked"]` and `["locked","locked"]` today.

root_cause.summary: The RK-S0263 fix was never applied to product code: `advance()` in src/process/engine.ts (lines ~768-772) still wraps the ENTIRE `advanceUnlocked` call — including the command gate's `{{redkiln}} verify` shell-out — in `withWriteLock`, and `AdvanceOptions` has no `preflightOnly` field or unlocked pre-flight pass. The shared cross-worktree write lock is therefore still held for the full duration of the gate command, which is the stall the story was supposed to remove.

hypothesis.summary: Grepped the tree for every identifier the implementation report claims to have added (`preflightOnly`, `preflightStage`, `gateMemoUsable`, `isMemoizedVerifyGate`, `headResolves`): zero hits in src/, dist/, or test/ — only in the spec's own prose. `src/process/engine.ts:768-772` is byte-identical to the pre-fix snippet the spec quotes; the claimed `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` does not exist; CHANGELOG's Unreleased section has no entry; working tree is clean at the single `advance to implement` commit. Then I confirmed the behaviour rather than inferring it: a temporary probe test declared the repo's `verify.affected_gate` as a script that records whether the shared write-lock directory (`<git-common-dir>/redkiln/.write.lock`) exists at the moment it executes, and drove a real `advance --apply` across the memoized `{{redkiln}} verify --grain story` gate on a git-identified tree with no `--fresh`/`REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE`. Passing gate: probe recorded `locked`. Failing gate: `locked,locked` (both the run and the flake-tolerance re-run), i.e. the lock is entered and held before the GateError propagates. That directly falsifies AC-001 and AC-002. The defect originates in `advance()`'s lock wrapping in src/process/engine.ts; gates.ts, verify-cache.ts and lock.ts are unmodified and, per the spec, correctly so. Probe file was deleted; tree left clean.

hypothesis.summary: I read the two files the spec froze the change to and found none of the described edits. Repo-wide grep for dod_owner/dodOwner matches only the spec document — no src, test, fixture, or CHANGELOG hits — and the git tree is clean at the single 'advance to implement' commit, so nothing is uncommitted. I then wrote and ran my own probe test: it built the index over the status fixture with RK-P0001 marked frontmatter `terminal: true` and RK-P0002 `terminal: false`; PRAGMA table_info(items) has no dod_owner column, ItemProjection's key list ends at blockedBy with no dodOwner, and both projects report terminal:false with dodOwner undefined — exactly the collision issue #82 describes, still unfixed. The claimed AC-001..AC-005 describes in test/queries-status.test.ts and the four new dod_owner cases in test/index-build.test.ts do not exist, and the fixtures said to have gained explicit `terminal:` frontmatter have none. The defect originates in the index write path (build.ts never captures the frontmatter value) and the read projection (queries.ts never exposes it); src/cli/status.ts is only where it is observed, since it passes q.items() through generically.

findings.claim: The release path makes exactly one rmdirSync attempt with no bounded retry, so a transient EBUSY strands the lock directory.
findings.rationale: I wrote and ran an independent vitest probe mocking node:fs rmdirSync to fail twice then succeed, and observed the call counter land on exactly 1 with the lock directory still on disk. This is a direct observation of the fault, not an inference from reading code.

repro.expected_when_met: rmdirSync called more than once (retry absorbs the two transient failures), lock directory gone (existsSync === false), and stderr empty.
repro.observed: [PROBE-A] rmdirSync calls = 1 | lockdir still exists = true | stderr = ""  -> AssertionError: expected 1 to be greater than 1

findings.claim: When rmdirSync fails on every attempt the release is completely silent — no `redkiln: warning:` is written to stderr naming the lock path.

repro.expected_when_met: stderr contains exactly one `redkiln: warning:` line naming the lock path, and the wrapped call still returns the critical section's value without throwing.
repro.observed: [PROBE-B] rmdirSync calls = 1 | stderr = ""  -> AssertionError: expected '' to contain 'redkiln: warning:'. The critical section's return value did come through correctly ('value'), so only the warning half of AC-002 is missing.

findings.claim: A fully sequential second withIdLock immediately after one transient release failure throws LockTimeoutError (EC-001) — the issue's exact repro shape reproduces at HEAD.
findings.rationale: I injected a single transient EBUSY on the first release and then awaited a second, strictly sequential withIdLock; it rejected with LockTimeoutError after burning the whole timeoutMs against a lock whose owner had already exited. Directly watched the reported fault.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/zzz-probe.test.ts  # probe: spec.md = '## PR boundary' -> '### Explicitly not in this PR' (fence forbidden/) -> '### In this PR' (fence allowed/); change allowed/x.txt
repro.expected_when_met: code= 0, pass= true — the change to `allowed/` is in-boundary and `forbidden/` declares nothing. This is what the same probe printed after I added the negation-subheading skip.
repro.observed: PROBE-017 code= 1 ran= true pass= false; detail= "changed outside declared boundary: allowed/x.txt; declared but matched no changed file: forbidden/"

findings.claim: The hypothesis's corroborating claim that "the implementation report cites them by line number" is false — none of `negatedAt`, `PATH_FENCE_INFO`, `NEGATION_SUBHEADING` appears anywhere in the repository, including the implementation report, which is an unfilled skeleton.
findings.rationale: I ran the grep across the whole worktree (excluding node_modules and .git) and read the implementation report in full. The report's TDD-evidence and Commits tables are empty and its only prose note concerns AC-014; there is no line-number citation of any guard. The claim is offered as evidence for the root cause but does not exist.

repro.command: grep -rn "negatedAt\|PATH_FENCE_INFO\|NEGATION_SUBHEADING\|fenceInfo\|infoString" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git
repro.expected_when_met: If the report cited the guards by line number, the grep would return hits in .bklg/support/issue-146-147-story-gate/issue-146-147-boundary-window/implementation-report.md.
repro.observed: No matches anywhere in the repository. implementation-report.md (61 lines) contains no occurrence of "guard", "AC-016", "AC-017", "AC-018", or any `verify.ts:<line>` citation.

findings.claim: The disproved compatibility claim is still present in CHANGELOG.md and duplicated in the `sectionPatterns` docstring, and the root cause's `files` list names only src/store/verify.ts, so a fix confined to the named file cannot satisfy AC-018.
findings.rationale: AC-018's stated acceptance is textual ("no occurrence of the 'can only widen … never narrow' claim survives in CHANGELOG.md"). I read both surfaces and confirmed the claim survives verbatim in CHANGELOG.md:61-62 and in src/store/verify.ts:568-573 — and my AC-016 repro disproves it. The hypothesis acknowledges the CHANGELOG miss but excludes the file from the root-cause set, which makes the set incomplete as a fix surface even if defensible as an origin claim.

repro.command: grep -n "widen" CHANGELOG.md; sed -n '50,62p' CHANGELOG.md; sed -n '568,573p' src/store/verify.ts
repro.expected_when_met: Neither surface carries the "can only widen … never narrow" guarantee; both state the real guarantee and name the advisory→patterns transition, per the spec's own corrected Compatibility note.
repro.observed: CHANGELOG.md:61-62 still reads "This can only widen a declared boundary, never narrow one — no spec that passes `boundary` today can start failing it.", and the same sentence appears in the sectionPatterns docstring at src/store/verify.ts:568-573.

findings.claim: The AC-014 assertion pins that a prohibition sentence survives inside the COMMIT step, not the requirement's stated property that the workflow contains no `redkiln advance`/`redkiln new`.
findings.rationale: The test file itself documents the substitution ("File-wide absence is NOT proven here, and cannot be"). I verified the substance is honest — all 7 `redkiln advance` and 2 `redkiln new` occurrences in workflows/forge-implement.js are prohibitions or comments, zero are invocations — so this is not a false claim, but the assertion is strictly narrower than the acceptance text it stands for, which is exactly narrowed-pin and not a reproduced fault.

repro.command: sed -n '419,445p' test/implement-contract.test.ts; grep -n "redkiln advance\|redkiln new" workflows/forge-implement.js
repro.expected_when_met: An assertion covering the property AC-014 names — e.g. that the file contains no invocation of `redkiln advance`/`redkiln new` (as opposed to prose mentioning them) — rather than the presence of one prohibition sentence in one step.
repro.observed: The AC-014 assertion is scoped to the numbered COMMIT step only: expect(commitStep).toMatch(/NEVER run[\s\S]{0,10}`?redkiln advance`?[\s\S]{0,10}`?redkiln new`?/). The workflow carries 9 occurrences of the two commands at lines 4, 313, 318, 1261, 1795, 2640, 2683 — all prohibitions or comments.

rubric.rationale: AC-001..AC-015 are implemented and covered by 75 green tests in test/verify.test.ts and test/implement-contract.test.ts. AC-016, AC-017 and AC-018 — the three criteria the spec amendment added — have neither implementation nor a single test: no fence info-string guard, no negation-subheading guard, and the CHANGELOG text AC-018 governs is unchanged. Three of eighteen criteria are entirely unaddressed, and they are the ones that bound the widened surface.

The proposed root cause is properly scoped: one file, one function, two named defects with line ranges that match the source exactly, and my mutation confirms a change confined to that function fixes both behaviours — so it is neither a symptom site nor an unactionable set. It loses a point because the files list omits CHANGELOG.md, which AC-018's own acceptance requires editing, and because the repository is a single squashed import commit so the diff cannot be audited against the spec's frozen PR boundary at all.

The existing #147/#146 tests are unusually well built — each carries an explicit MUTATION note, AC-003/AC-004 deliberately use tables rather than fences so the terminator is genuinely load-bearing, and there is a non-vacuity check on the COMMIT-step regex. Against that, three ACs have no test at all, AC-014's pin is an acknowledged substitution narrower than its requirement, and the discriminating test offered for this item was two probe files that were deleted, leaving nothing in the repo that can fail if the guards stay absent.

The gate is green — exit 0, 75/75 — but vacuously so. I implemented both missing guards, verified through a probe that behaviour genuinely changed on both cases, and the same command returned exit 0 / 75 passed unchanged. A gate that reports the same result with and without the defect is not evidence of the property it is cited for.

This is not a hypothetical risk, it is a reproduced live regression against the repository's own corpus. A spec that passes today at exit 0 with a non-blocking advisory becomes a hard boundary failure declaring `if (mode === 'worktree') return absolute(p) && !under(p, root);` as a path, and an exclusion list written first inverts the declared boundary so the story's real in-scope change is reported as the stray. The shipped CHANGELOG note simultaneously promises operators that neither can happen.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:
- it names a symptom, not the origin: the file where the wrong value is PRINTED rather than where it is computed
- it names the right area but the wrong file, or a set so broad it is not actionable

- the evidence offered does not support the claim, even though the claim may happen to be true

findings.rationale: I ran the exact named command three times — fault present, with a deliberately nonsense filter, and with the proposed fix applied to workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js — and observed byte-identical output (34 skipped, exit 0) each time. That is direct observation of non-discrimination, not inference.

root_cause.summary: workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js's Stage 1 project-charter prompt (lines 714-715) still tells the agent to put a relative link to `${DIR}/_plan.md` in the charter's `## Companions` section, but that rollup is only written later by the separate forge-plan-prds.js workflow (PLAN_PATH, line 371) — so every charter cites a dead link that the same run's Stage 5 dead-anchor check (item 4) is guaranteed to flag. The compensating step is also missing: forge-plan-prds.js never appends the `../_plan.md` companion link to each projectItemPath(s) after `verdict.planWritten === true` is confirmed.

hypothesis.summary: The #74 fix never landed in this checkout; the defect sits exactly where the issue located it. Direct evidence: (1) forge-plan-briefs.js:714-715 still instructs the Stage 1 charter agent to link "the rollup ${DIR}/_plan.md" — running the report's own AC-001 slice assertion returns true for /_plan\.md/; (2) repo-wide grep for `link-plan` (workflows, test, src, md, tiers.mjs) returns nothing, so forge-plan-prds.js has no planWritten-gated companion-link step between the re-verify reassignment (line 1262) and the Manifest block (1266); (3) the claimed new tests do not exist — plan-contract.test.ts runs 34 tests and plan-dag.test.ts runs 25 (report claims 35 and 28, i.e. exactly the 1+3 new tests missing), and CHANGELOG.md has no #74 entry; (4) diffing this tree's forge-plan-prds.js against the pre-#79 sibling snapshot shows only #79's work, and against a later snapshot shows the real #74 block as a pure addition, so no other mutation is confounding the reading. Consequence at runtime: Stage 1 authors `../_plan.md` in ${projectDir(p)}/project.md, and forge-plan-briefs.js's own Stage 5 check 4 (lines 941-946) resolves relative links in artifacts under ${projectDir(p)}/ against the citing file's directory, guaranteeing a self-inflicted deadAnchors entry in the same run.

hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/plan-contract.test.ts -t "step 9 authors discover.md and ticks gates/discover"

root_cause.summary: commands/plan.md step 9 still tells the orchestrator to run `redkiln advance <STORY-ID> --to spec --apply` directly after `redkiln new story`, with no sub-step that authors the rendered discover.md or ticks the four `## Gate: Discover` boxes. Because processes/story.yaml's discover stage carries a hard-blocking `gates/discover` checklist gate that renders fully unticked, the literal instruction cannot succeed on a standard-tier story. The claimed fix (mirroring commands/initiative.md's gates/intake handling) is simply absent from this checkout.

hypothesis.summary: I reproduced the reported symptom end-to-end rather than inferring it: scaffolded a scratch repo with this build's bin/redkiln.mjs, created a standard-tier story, and ran step 9's literal command — `redkiln advance RK-S0001 --to spec --apply` exits 1 with \"checklist gate 'gates/discover' failed: 4 required item(s) not ticked\", the freshly rendered discover.md being the untouched template. A story-lite control advanced intake -> spec cleanly (exit 0), isolating the failure to the standard-tier discover gate. Grepping commands/plan.md for `discover` returns only the pre-fix lines 279-288: no authoring sub-step, no `gates/discover`, no `## Gate: Discover`, no `adopt --templates` fallback; and no compensating instruction exists anywhere in commands/, workflows/, agents/ or skills/. commands/initiative.md:159-160 still carries the analogous gates/intake pattern the fix was supposed to mirror, so the mirroring was never done. The defect is silent because the accompanying assertions were never added: test/plan-contract.test.ts holds 26 tests, none referencing gates/discover, and runs 26/26 green — contradicting the report's claimed 34/34 and red->green cycle. CHANGELOG.md has no #81 entry. Diffing against the sibling e3-clean-issue-81 fixture confirms the exact shape: the only deltas are the ~20-line plan.md sub-step, the two new describe blocks, and the changelog entry; src/process/gates.ts, processes/story.yaml and templates/gates/discover.md are byte-identical, so the engine and pack are correct as designed and the defect lives solely in the prescriptive document. A discriminating test is the AC-001 block asserting that step 9's text slice (from \"9. **scaffold the stories\" to \"10. **launch stage b-2\") matches /gates\\/discover/ and that its index precedes that of \"--to spec --apply\" — red on this tree, green once step 9 carries the sub-step.

digest.summary: The change described in the implementation report was never applied to this checkout. The working tree is clean at the single commit `3484359 "advance to implement"`, with no other branches/stashes/worktrees, and the on-disk `implementation-report.md` is the blank rendered template rather than the filled report quoted in the item. So the item advanced into `implement` and success was reported without any work being done. The wrong behaviour therefore still originates exactly where issue #70 put it — the "Invoking the workflow" note and every `scriptPath: '<$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>/workflows/forge-*.js'` placeholder in the 6 `commands/*.md` prompt files — plus the absence of the CLI-owned resolution mechanism (`bundledWorkflowsDir()` in `src/store/paths.ts`, the handler `src/cli/workflow-root.ts`, and its registration in `src/cli/commands.ts` / `src/cli/index.ts`) that was supposed to replace it.

I verified directly: `src/cli/workflow-root.ts` and `test/workflow-root.test.ts` do not exist; `src/store/paths.ts` exports no `bundledWorkflowsDir` (only assetRoot/bundledProcessesDir/bundledTemplatesDir/bundledKbSkeletonDir/targetPath/assertSegment/isArchivedPath); `src/cli/commands.ts`'s COMMANDS array ends at `record-links` and `src/cli/index.ts`'s dispatch switch has no `workflow-root` case, so `node bin/redkiln.mjs workflow-root` prints "unknown command 'workflow-root'" and exits 1; `grep -rn CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT commands/` still returns 20 matches across exactly the 6 files the spec named (AC-003 fails); `vitest run test/flag-projection.test.ts` yields 69 tests with no `workflow-root` case (contradicting the AC-005 claim); `docs/.../reference/cli.mdx` goes straight from `## record-links` to `## See also`; CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` has no `Added` entry and no mention of #70. The working tree is clean at the single commit `3484359 "advance to implement"`, with no other branches/stashes/worktrees, and the on-disk `implementation-report.md` is the blank rendered template rather than the filled report quoted in the item. So the item advanced into `implement` and success was reported without any work being done. The wrong behaviour therefore still originates exactly where issue #70 put it — the "Invoking the workflow" note and every `scriptPath: '<$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>/workflows/forge-*.js'` placeholder in the 6 `commands/*.md` prompt files — plus the absence of the CLI-owned resolution mechanism (`bundledWorkflowsDir()` in `src/store/paths.ts`, the handler `src/cli/workflow-root.ts`, and its registration in `src/cli/commands.ts` / `src/cli/index.ts`) that was supposed to replace it.

I reproduced the fault directly: with a `_review.md` planted in the story's own directory, `advance --to g1 --commit` commits only spec.md/story.md/telemetry and leaves `_review.md` untracked while reporting success. I then discriminated the location: patching ONLY the staged-pathspec computation in `src/cli/advance.ts` (adding the item's directory alongside `writtenPaths`, existence-filtered) turned that repro green while the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression and the other five tests stayed green — proving `commit()` in `src/git/index.ts` already accepts a directory pathspec and is not the defect, and that the wrong behaviour originates in the CLI's staging set. `src/process/engine.ts` is the secondary half: it is where the item directory (`located.dir`) is known and where `AdvanceResult`/`BlockedWalkError` fail to carry it, which is why the CLI can only guess. The silence itself is guarded by the existing "narrow staging" test, which asserts precisely the buggy policy — a test-policy problem, not the origin of the behaviour.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` computes its staged pathspec set as `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` (src/cli/advance.ts:121-129, and identically `err.writtenPaths` in the BlockedWalkError catch at ~line 220), i.e. only the files THIS transition wrote. Companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_discovery/` corpus, a `_review.md`) are therefore never staged and stay untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. findings.claim: The named discriminating command selects zero tests and exits 0 identically whether the fault is present or fixed, so it discriminates nothing.
findings.rationale: I ran the exact recorded command verbatim against the unmodified (faulty) tree and again against a tree where I had applied the staging fix. Both produced '6 tests | 6 skipped', 'Test Files 1 skipped (1)', exit 0. That is direct observation of non-discrimination, not an inference about the pattern syntax. Root cause of the non-selection: vitest treats -t as a regex, so the literal parentheses in 'commit (narrow staging)' become a capture group and the pattern demands the text 'commit narrow staging', which no test name contains. Escaping them (\(narrow staging\)) selects the test and it PASSES on the faulty tree and FAILS under the fix - the opposite polarity to the one asserted in the write-up.

The submitted artifact for that exact command is exit 0, passed:true, 6 skipped. I confirmed the quoted assertion text can only come from a separately-authored INVERTED probe (my own inverted probe emits precisely that string), not from the un-inverted test that ships in the repo and not from the command as recorded. The claim happens to be true about the code, but the cited evidence is from a different artifact than the one named.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/_probe-ac001.test.ts   # my inverted AC-001 probe, then compare to the recorded run of the un-inverted test
repro.expected_when_met: The failure text quoted as evidence is produced by the command that was actually named and run, in the state that was actually recorded.
repro.observed: My inverted probe fails with exactly "expected '.bklg/foundation/cutover/root/spec.md…' to contain '_review.md'". The recorded command for the shipped un-inverted test reports 6 skipped / exit 0 and emits no assertion output at all.

findings.claim: src/process/engine.ts is named as a root-cause file, but the fault is fully corrected by editing src/cli/advance.ts alone, so engine.ts is a design-ergonomics concern rather than an origin of the wrong value.
findings.rationale: I applied a single-file patch to src/cli/advance.ts that derives the item directory from result.writtenPaths and prepends it to the staged pathspec set, leaving src/process/engine.ts completely untouched. AC-001 (companion _review.md and _discovery/notes.md land in the commit), AC-002 (sibling item's untracked file stays out) and AC-003 (telemetry partition still committed) all passed. This is observation, not argument: the missing AdvanceResult.itemDir field is a cleanliness improvement the spec elected, not the site where the wrong pathspec set is computed. Naming it as a root-cause file makes the root cause broader than the evidence supports.

repro.command:

npx vitest run test/_probe-ac001.test.ts
repro.expected_when_met: If engine.ts were causally part of the root cause, the fault would persist or the ACs would remain unsatisfiable without changing it.
repro.observed: 3 passed (3) with src/process/engine.ts unmodified. Committed set became .bklg/.../_discovery/notes.md, _review.md, spec.md, story.md, telemetry jsonl; 'git status --porcelain -- .bklg' empty.

findings.claim: The existing "narrow staging" test asserts the faulty behaviour as intended policy, so the whole suite is green while the fault is present and no gate detects it.
findings.rationale: test/advance-git-commit.test.ts:188-201 plants _review.md in the item's OWN directory (storyDir()) and asserts it stays OUT of the commit and remains untracked. The requirement behind that test - per its own name and comment - is that an UNRELATED sibling is not swept in, a boundary that AC-002 covers and that I confirmed still holds under the fix. The test pins a strictly narrower and in fact contradictory policy: it forbids staging the item's own companion artifacts, which is exactly the #77 defect. I ran the full suite on the unmodified tree: 92 files / 1877 tests all pass with the fault live. This is a narrowed-pin rather than mutation-survived because the test is not merely insensitive - it actively encodes the wrong requirement.

repro.command: npx vitest run   # full suite on unmodified HEAD
repro.expected_when_met: A test guarding AC-002's boundary would plant the stray file in a DIFFERENT item's directory, so the suite would go red on the AC-001 defect instead of certifying it.
repro.observed: Test Files 92 passed (92); Tests 1877 passed (1877) - fully green while advance --commit demonstrably leaves companion artifacts untracked behind a gitCommitted:true report.

rubric.rationale: The proposal correctly identifies the origin of the wrong value (the staged pathspec set at src/cli/advance.ts:121-129) and I independently reproduced the fault and confirmed a single-site patch satisfies AC-001, AC-002 and AC-003. Marked down because the verification offered for that coverage is vacuous - the named discriminating command executed zero tests - so none of the AC claims are actually evidenced by the submitted artifact.

Both named files sit inside the spec's frozen PR boundary, and the proposal correctly excludes src/git/index.ts's commit() after checking that git add already accepts a directory pathspec. Marked down because src/process/engine.ts is presented as part of the root cause when it is not causally necessary: I fixed the fault with advance.ts alone, making the two-file naming broader than the evidence supports.

The discriminating test as named and run selects nothing and returns 0 in both the faulty and fixed states, and the quoted failure message comes from a different artifact than the recorded run. Credit retained because the proposal does correctly and explicitly flag that the shipped narrow-staging test encodes the buggy policy and must be inverted rather than silently broken.

The recorded green is not a meaningful gate: exit 0 with 6/6 skipped is indistinguishable from a real pass in the harness output, and I reproduced that same green against a tree with the fix applied. The full suite is separately green (1877/1877) with the fault live, so no existing gate constrains this behaviour at all.

I exercised the risk surface of the proposed widening: the sibling-item boundary holds, the telemetry partition outside the item directory is still committed, and the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression stays green. Only the one deliberately-inverted test fails, matching the proposal's own account. Residual risk is that the fix's blast radius is only ever validated by tests the same change rewrites.

hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/advance-git-commit.test.ts -t "does not sweep an unrelated untracked sibling into the commit (narrow staging)" — invert it: after writing `_review.md` into `storyDir()` and running `advance <id> --to g1 --commit`, assert `git show --name-only HEAD` CONTAINS `_review.md` and `git status --porcelain -- .bklg` is empty. It fails today ("expected '.bklg/foundation/cutover/root/spec.md…' to contain '_review.md'") and passes as soon as the item directory joins the staged pathspecs in src/cli/advance.ts.

root_cause.summary: `advance --commit` computes its staged pathspec set as `result.writtenPaths.filter(existsSync)` (src/cli/advance.ts:121-129, and identically `err.writtenPaths` in the BlockedWalkError catch at ~line 220), i.e. only the files THIS transition wrote. Companion artifacts already sitting in the item's own directory (a `_discovery/` corpus, a `_review.md`) are therefore never staged and stay untracked behind a commit that reports `gitCommitted: true`. The engine compounds this by not exposing the item's directory at all: `AdvanceResult`/`BlockedWalkError` (src/process/engine.ts:151-227) carry `writtenPaths` but no `itemDir` from the `located = locateItemIn(...)` result, so the CLI has no clean way to widen staging to the one item folder.

hypothesis.summary: The repository is at the pre-implementation state for RK-S0234: nothing from the reported fix exists in `src` (no `itemDir` on `AdvanceResult`/`BlockedWalkError`, both commit sites in `src/cli/advance.ts` still stage `writtenPaths` alone, no #77 CHANGELOG entry, and `test/advance-git-commit.test.ts` still contains the un-inverted 6 tests). I confirmed the sibling fixtures that postdate #77 upstream do carry `[result.itemDir, ...result.writtenPaths]`, so that is the shape of the real fix. I reproduced the fault directly: with a `_review.md` planted in the story's own directory, `advance --to g1 --commit` commits only spec.md/story.md/telemetry and leaves `_review.md` untracked while reporting success. I then discriminated the location: patching ONLY the staged-pathspec computation in `src/cli/advance.ts` (adding the item's directory alongside `writtenPaths`, existence-filtered) turned that repro green while the RK-N0001 gitignored-path regression and the other five tests stayed green — proving `commit()` in `src/git/index.ts` already accepts a directory pathspec and is not the defect, and that the wrong behaviour originates in the CLI's staging set. `src/process/engine.ts` is the secondary half: it is where the item directory (`located.dir`) is known and where `AdvanceResult`/`BlockedWalkError` fail to carry it, which is why the CLI can only guess. The silence itself is guarded by the existing "narrow staging" test, which asserts precisely the buggy policy — a test-policy problem, not the origin of the behaviour.

repro.observed: 1 commit; 590 files in HEAD; 120 under .bklg/ — the commit imports the entire tree (.claude-plugin, .github, src, dist, test, ...), not just backlog docs.

rubric.rationale: The hypothesis accounts for every AC that actually fails and explains the ones that pass. I confirmed by execution: AC-001, AC-002, AC-005 and EC-001 fail against this checkout, AC-003/AC-004/NF-002 and the four carve-outs pass trivially because single-pass code satisfies them by construction. Swapping in the clean src/process/engine.ts alone turned all 12 green, so the named cause explains 100% of the failing surface with nothing left over.

The named file set is exactly one file, src/process/engine.ts, which is the first row of the spec's frozen PR boundary. A recursive diff against the clean reference shows engine.ts is the only source file that differs (the rest are the test artifact, CHANGELOG, dist bundles and a report stub), so the claim is neither too broad nor displaced into an adjacent module — gates.ts, verify-cache.ts and lock.ts are byte-identical to the fixed reference, correctly ruled out. Nothing in the working tree was modified by my review; the mutation was reverted and git status is empty.

The test the hypothesis nominates as discriminating is absent from the checkout, and the recorded run terminates in vitest's file-glob filter with "No test files found" before loading any product code — an outcome invariant to the hypothesis. The investigator disclosed this and used a copied reference file instead, whose 4/12 result I reproduced exactly, so the underlying reasoning is sound; but the gate as named and recorded proves nothing, and the spec's required regression file at test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts does not exist here.

The recorded discriminating gate exits non-zero for a reason unrelated to the fault (missing file), which is red-for-the-wrong-reason rather than a meaningful signal. When I supplied the reference test the suite is genuinely red at 4 failed / 8 passed, and goes 12/12 green under the single-file mutation — so a real gate exists, it just is not the one that was run. I did not run the full pnpm test suite, so repo-wide greenness is unestablished either way.

The mutation evidence is reassuring: replacing only src/process/engine.ts flips all four failures without touching gates.ts, verify-cache.ts or lock.ts, and the reference test explicitly pins the risky adjacencies (multi-hop --to walk incremental commits, non-memoized run: gates, --fresh, REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE, no-HEAD trees) which all passed. Held back from 3 because I did not run the full suite after the mutation, and because dist/ remains stale relative to a fixed src, which NF-001 makes part of the shipping requirement.

You are given their hypothesis and the result of the discriminating test they named. You have the repository. Check the claim yourself rather than reasoning about it.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:
- it names a symptom, not the origin: the file where the wrong value is PRINTED rather than where it is computed
- it names the right area but the wrong file, or a set so broad it is not actionable
- the discriminating test does not in fact discriminate: it would pass or fail the same way either way
- the evidence offered does not support the claim, even though the claim may happen to be true

Classify every finding by the evidence you actually have. `reproduced` means you ran something and watched it behave as you describe. `mutation-survived` means you changed a behaviour and the suite stayed green. `narrowed-pin` means a test pins a narrower claim than the requirement behind it. `advisory` is anything you could not evidence at that bar — use it honestly rather than inflating a hunch.

You return no verdict. It is computed from your findings.","tools":["Read","Bash","StructuredOutput"],"model":"opus","effort":"xhigh"}}

rubric.rationale: The hypothesis names the true origin and a sufficient, minimal file set: patching only src/index/build.ts and src/index/queries.ts made AC-001..AC-004 hold end-to-end (projection AND `status --json`), with src/cli/status.ts confirmed a generic passthrough (`items: q.items()` + JSON.stringify) and src/schema/item.ts:133 confirmed correct. Marked down because none of AC-001..AC-004 is actually pinned by any surviving test — the recorded run covers zero of them.

The investigator stayed inside the spec's frozen surface and left the tree clean (git status --porcelain empty at 7084f94, probe deleted). But the boundary they endorsed is provably too narrow: the spec-shaped column addition reds test/read-side-pack.test.ts:391, which is text-coupled to the exact SCHEMA line and is not an allowed path.

The discriminating test is void as evidence: test/queries-status.test.ts has no dodOwner assertion and returns 26/26 on both sides of the fix (I verified both sides). The one assertion that did discriminate was written as a throwaway and deleted, so the repo retains nothing that distinguishes fixed from broken. The claim happens to be true; the offered evidence does not support it.

The recorded green run proves only that an unrelated suite passes. Worse, the real gate is not green under the spec'd change: full `npx vitest run` with the additive column gave `1 failed | 1851 passed`, EXIT=1, versus a green baseline for that same file after revert.

The additive direction is genuinely low-blast-radius — ItemProjection.terminal/isTerminal untouched, readyQueue unaffected, and INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION = shortDigest(SCHEMA) invalidates stale caches automatically (89 of 91 suites plus index-build's subset-based PRAGMA table_info assertion stayed green). The residual risk is the schema-text-literal coupling in read-side-pack.test.ts, which the hypothesis did not anticipate.

findings.claim: The named discriminating test does not discriminate: `test/queries-status.test.ts` contains zero `dodOwner` assertions and passes 26/26 identically whether the fix is present or absent.
findings.rationale: I did not merely reason about it: I implemented the spec'd behaviour (dod_owner column + binding in build.ts, dodOwner in ItemProjection/SELECT/map in queries.ts), then re-ran the exact recorded command. The suite stayed green with the same 26/26 count, so the artifact submitted as the discriminator is invariant to the fault. `grep -n "dodOwner" test/queries-status.test.ts` returns nothing; the only assertion that actually discriminated lived in a temporary probe the investigator deleted, so no discriminating evidence survives in the repo. The root-cause claim itself is correct — my in-boundary patch made a probe asserting `dodOwner === true` for RK-P0001 and `null` for RK-S0001 go from failing to passing — but this test cannot establish it.

repro.command: npx vitest run test/queries-status.test.ts   # pre-fix: 26 passed. Then patch build.ts (dod_owner column + `data.type === "project" ? ((data.terminal ?? true) ? 1 : 0) : null` binding) and queries.ts (dodOwner in ItemProjection, SELECT, row map) and re-run the identical command.
repro.expected_when_met: The named file would contain assertions on `dodOwner` for RK-P0001 (true), a `terminal: false` project (false) and non-project items (null), so the recorded run would have been RED before the fix and only turn green after it — i.e. the exit code would flip across the fix, not stay 0 on both sides.
repro.observed: Pre-fix: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 26 passed (26)`. Post-fix: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 26 passed (26)`. A separate throwaway probe (test/zz-probe-issue82.test.ts) showed the real difference: pre-fix `AssertionError: expected undefined to be true` and projection keys `...,slice,terminal,pickable,gateOpen,ready,blockedBy` with no dodOwner; post-fix `PROBE P0001.terminal = false dodOwner = true` and green.

findings.claim: The frozen change surface named in the root cause is incomplete: a straightforward in-boundary implementation of the spec'd `dod_owner` column reds `test/read-side-pack.test.ts:391`, a file the boundary forbids touching, so the merge gate (`pnpm test`) does not stay green.
findings.rationale: I ran the whole suite with the patch applied and watched it fail, then reverted and ran the same file alone to confirm the failure is caused by the column and is not pre-existing. `test/read-side-pack.test.ts:386-391` string-replaces the literal `"  terminal INTEGER, pickable INTEGER, gate_open INTEGER,\n  tier TEXT, archetype TEXT, slice TEXT\n"` out of `SCHEMA` and asserts `old !== SCHEMA`; any column appended to (or after) that `slice TEXT` line makes the replace a no-op. This is implementation-placement-dependent — putting `dod_owner` earlier in the table would dodge it — but nothing in the hypothesis or spec says so, and the naive reading of "SCHEMA gains one nullable column" breaks a file outside the five allowed paths.

repro.command: npx vitest run   # with dod_owner appended to the `tier TEXT, archetype TEXT, slice TEXT` line of SCHEMA; then `git checkout -- src/index/build.ts src/index/queries.ts && npx vitest run test/read-side-pack.test.ts`
repro.expected_when_met: The full suite stays green with the new column in place, with no edit needed to any file outside the frozen list (src/index/build.ts, src/index/queries.ts, test/index-build.test.ts, test/queries-status.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md).
repro.observed: With the fix: `Test Files 1 failed | 90 passed (91) / Tests 1 failed | 1851 passed (1852)`, EXIT=1 — `FAIL test/read-side-pack.test.ts > AC-READ-SCHEMA-BUMP ... AssertionError: expected '\nDROP TABLE IF EXISTS items;…' not to be '\nDROP TABLE IF EXISTS items;…'` at line 391. Reverted baseline: `test/read-side-pack.test.ts` 14 passed.

findings.claim: No fixture in the frozen boundary carries `terminal: false`, so AC-002/AC-004 cannot be verified against the committed fixture set without either editing `test/fixtures/status/**` (outside the boundary) or synthesising frontmatter inside the test.
findings.rationale: I confirmed the gap by reading all three fixture projects (RK-P0001/2/3 in test/fixtures/status/.bklg) — none has a `terminal:` key — and the boundary lists only two src files, two test files and CHANGELOG.md. I am filing this as advisory rather than reproduced because I showed it is surmountable in-file: my probe copied the fixture to a temp dir and injected `terminal: false` into RK-P0002 at runtime, and AC-002/AC-004 then held (`P0001 terminal=false dodOwner=true | P0002 terminal=false dodOwner=false | I0001 dodOwner=null`). It is a boundary hazard for the implementer, not a defect in the root cause.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:

findings.rationale: I ran the whole suite with the patch applied and watched it fail, then reverted and ran the same file alone to confirm the failure is caused by the column and is not pre-existing. `test/read-side-pack.test.ts:386-391` string-replaces the literal `"  terminal INTEGER, pickable INTEGER, gate_open INTEGER,\n  tier TEXT, archetype TEXT, slice TEXT\n"` out of `SCHEMA` and asserts `old !== SCHEMA`; any column appended to (or after) that `slice TEXT` line makes the replace a no-op. This is implementation-placement-dependent — putting `dod_owner` earlier in the table would dodge it — but nothing in the hypothesis or spec says so, and the naive reading of "SCHEMA gains one nullable column" breaks a file outside the five allowed paths.

I am filing this as advisory rather than reproduced because I showed it is surmountable in-file: my probe copied the fixture to a temp dir and injected `terminal: false` into RK-P0002 at runtime, and AC-002/AC-004 then held (`P0001 terminal=false dodOwner=true | P0002 terminal=false dodOwner=false | I0001 dodOwner=null`). rubric.rationale: The hypothesis names the true origin and a sufficient, minimal file set: patching only src/index/build.ts and src/index/queries.ts made AC-001..AC-004 hold end-to-end (projection AND `status --json`), with src/cli/status.ts confirmed a generic passthrough (`items: q.items()` + JSON.stringify) and src/schema/item.ts:133 confirmed correct. Marked down because none of AC-001..AC-004 is actually pinned by any surviving test — the recorded run covers zero of them.

The investigator stayed inside the spec's frozen surface and left the tree clean (git status --porcelain empty at 7084f94, probe deleted). But the boundary they endorsed is provably too narrow: the spec-shaped column addition reds test/read-side-pack.test.ts:391, which is text-coupled to the exact SCHEMA line and is not an allowed path.

The discriminating test is void as evidence: test/queries-status.test.ts has no dodOwner assertion and returns 26/26 on both sides of the fix (I verified both sides). The one assertion that did discriminate was written as a throwaway and deleted, so the repo retains nothing that distinguishes fixed from broken. The claim happens to be true; the offered evidence does not support it.

The recorded green run proves only that an unrelated suite passes. Worse, the real gate is not green under the spec'd change: full `npx vitest run` with the additive column gave `1 failed | 1851 passed`, EXIT=1, versus a green baseline for that same file after revert.

The additive direction is genuinely low-blast-radius — ItemProjection.terminal/isTerminal untouched, readyQueue unaffected, and INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION = shortDigest(SCHEMA) invalidates stale caches automatically (89 of 91 suites plus index-build's subset-based PRAGMA table_info assertion stayed green). The residual risk is the schema-text-literal coupling in read-side-pack.test.ts, which the hypothesis did not anticipate.

hypothesis.discriminating_test: test/queries-status.test.ts — build the status fixture index and assert `openQueries(db).items().find(i => i.id === "RK-P0001").dodOwner === true` and `…find("RK-S0001").dodOwner === null`; today both read `undefined` (verified with a temporary probe test: "expected undefined to be true").

root_cause.summary: The spec'd additive fix was never implemented: `src/index/build.ts` still has no `dod_owner` column in `SCHEMA` and `insertItems` never binds the project frontmatter `terminal` (DoD-owner) value — only the pack-derived lifecycle `isTerminalFor` result — and `src/index/queries.ts`'s `ItemProjection`/`items()` neither selects nor exposes `dodOwner`. `status --json` therefore still reports only the lifecycle `terminal` flag, leaving the #82 collision exactly as reported.

hypothesis.summary: Read the two files the spec froze as the change surface. `SCHEMA` in src/index/build.ts (line 129) still ends `terminal INTEGER, pickable INTEGER, gate_open INTEGER, tier/archetype/slice` with no `dod_owner`, and `insertItems` binds 24 parameters, none derived from `data.terminal` — only `isTerminalFor(data)` (the pack lifecycle fact). `ItemProjection` in src/index/queries.ts (326-359) has no `dodOwner`, and `items()`'s SELECT (702-705) and projection map (719-745) omit it. Confirmed at runtime: `redkiln status --json` items have no `dodOwner` key, and `PRAGMA table_info(items)` on the built index shows 24 columns with no `dod_owner`. A temporary probe test asserting `dodOwner === true` for the fixture project RK-P0001 failed with `expected undefined to be true`, then I deleted it (tree clean). The reported test/fixture/CHANGELOG changes are also absent (48 tests in the two named suites, all pre-existing and green; fixtures carry no `terminal:` frontmatter; no #82 CHANGELOG entry; the in-repo implementation-report.md is still the blank template). The defect is the missing indexing + projection of the frontmatter DoD-owner field, and it lives in those two src files — not in status.ts (which passes the projection through generically) or schema/item.ts (the frontmatter field is correct) or store/verify.ts (reads frontmatter directly).

root_cause.summary: The #79 fix was never applied: `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` still computes `const verified = verdict?.pass === true && DAG.acyclic && dagGaps.length === 0` (:1241) with no confirmation that `_plan.md` was written, `VERIFY_SCHEMA` (:546-572) has no required `planWritten` attestation (only the unchecked `planPath` string), and neither the `verify-plan` (:1107-1147) nor the `re-verify:plan` (:1199-1231) prompt requires a filesystem postcondition for the rollup (VERIFY_CHECKS 4b at :1078 covers the project artifacts but not `_plan.md`). A `pass: true` self-report over an unwritten rollup therefore still yields `verified: true` / `_obs.outcome: completed`.

digest.summary: I read the three anchor regions of workflows/forge-plan-prds.js named by the spec and grepped the whole repo for `planWritten`: it occurs only inside the spec document — zero occurrences in the workflow, test/plan-dag.test.ts, test/helpers/workflow-harness.ts, or CHANGELOG.md. Line 1241 is verbatim the pre-fix `verified` expression; VERIFY_SCHEMA's `required` list is unchanged (`pass`, `planPath`, `gaps`); VERIFY_CHECKS' artifact postcondition (4b) enumerates project.md/_decomposition.md/_grounding.md/_storymap.md and omits _plan.md — the one artifact this verify stage itself authors. I then drove the real control flow through test/helpers/workflow-harness.ts with a DigestPatch setting `pass: true, planWritten: false` on both verify labels over a clean acyclic seed: the manifest returned `verified: true` and `_obs.outcome: "completed"`, so AC-001 fails against this tree. The fault is silent — plan-dag is 21 tests (the report claims 25) and plan-dag/workflow-smoke/fanout-cap/workflow-model-tiers run 133/133 green. Several report claims are impossible against this tree (it cites :1276-1277 in a 1264-line file; the claimed AC-PW block at test/plan-dag.test.ts:287-347 is actually the pre-existing fix-#83 block; `run()` has no `patch` parameter; the on-disk .bklg implementation-report.md is a blank template; the only #79 mention in CHANGELOG.md is inside the #73 entry stating #79 is NOT touched). The origin of the wrong behaviour is the `verified` computation plus the schema/prompt pair feeding it, all inside workflows/forge-plan-prds.js; the missing tests are a detection gap, not the origin, so I did not list them.
