findings.rationale: Read directly and cross-checked against ground truth: coordinationDir at lock.ts:99-102 returns join(gitCommonDir(root), 'redkiln') inside a repo, which contradicts the ids.ts:5 comment. AC-005's own verification method is 'manual read', so a read is the intended bar here.

repro.command: sed -n '1,15p' src/store/ids.ts; sed -n '99,102p' src/store/lock.ts
repro.expected_when_met: ids.ts's header names `<git-common-dir>/redkiln/` (with the non-git `.redkiln/index/` fallback), matching coordinationDir.
repro.observed: ids.ts:5 — 'The lock is an atomic `mkdir` of `.redkiln/index/.id.lock`'; lock.ts:99-102 — `return common === null ? targetPath(root, TARGET.index) : join(common, "redkiln")`.

findings.claim: Part of the evidence cited for the root cause does not exist in the repository: the implementation report contains none of the claims attributed to it.
findings.rationale: The root cause's summary rests partly on rebutting an implement report that allegedly 'claims a shared releaseLock helper at lock.ts:183-208, constants at lock.ts:63-64, a new test/lock.test.ts, AC-003 cases at test/ids.test.ts:411-487'. I read the on-disk report and grepped the whole .bklg and .redkiln trees for those citations: the report is an unfilled template whose TDD-evidence, commits, changes and gates sections are empty tables, and none of the cited strings appear anywhere. The conclusion (nothing was implemented) is correct and I evidenced it independently above; this specific supporting evidence is not verifiable against the repo, which is the 'evidence offered does not support the claim' failure mode even where the claim is true.

repro.command: cat .bklg/support/fix-core-cli-schema/issue-66-id-lock-ec001-rmdir/implementation-report.md; grep -rn 'lock.ts:183\|lock.ts:63\|411-487\|releaseLock' .bklg .redkiln
repro.expected_when_met: The implement report would contain the line/file citations being rebutted, so that 'the report claims X; X does not exist' is a checkable statement.
repro.observed: Report is the blank template (empty '| AC | Test | Red -> Green |' and '| SHA | Subject |' rows, empty Changes/Gates/Notes sections). grep returns zero matches across .bklg and .redkiln.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001..AC-005 is met. I reproduced AC-001 (one rmdirSync call, lock dir stranded), AC-002 (zero stderr bytes on permanent failure), and AC-003 (next sequential acquisition throws LockTimeoutError after the full window) as live failures against the clean tree; AC-005's stale doc comment is still at ids.ts:5. AC-004 is 'met' only vacuously, since acquisition was never touched. No shared release helper, no retry budget constants, no warning path exist anywhere in the tree.

The frozen boundary permits src/store/lock.ts, src/store/ids.ts, test/ids.test.ts or test/lock.test.ts, and CHANGELOG.md. The working tree is clean at the single 'advance to implement' commit, so no file inside or outside the boundary was modified. Nothing was touched that should not have been. The named root-cause files (lock.ts, ids.ts) are both inside the declared boundary, so the diagnosis is actionable within it.

test/lock.test.ts does not exist and test/ids.test.ts is unchanged at 380 lines, ending at the pre-existing EC-001 acquisition suite. The named discriminating command is therefore not a test of the fix at all: I built the fixed world and it still printed 'No test files found, exiting with code 1' with exit 1, byte-identical to the broken world, so it cannot separate the two hypotheses. Separately, mutating release behaviour left 87 lock-adjacent tests green, confirming nothing pins this behaviour.

`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and every test file I ran passes on the clean tree (ids.test.ts 11/11; ids-worktrees, index-concurrency, store-write, engine-advance 76/76). The gate is green, but vacuously so: it is green precisely because no code changed, and it stayed green under a behaviour-changing mutation of the release path, so greenness here carries no signal about the fix. I did not run the full `pnpm lint` or the complete ~90-file suite, hence not full marks.

Zero lines of production code were changed, so no regression can have been introduced; AC-004's requirement that acquisition/LockTimeoutError/the reentrancy `held` map be untouched is trivially satisfied. The risk in this tree is the unfixed defect persisting, not a regression. I also confirmed the intended fix shape is low-risk: with releaseLock applied, all 87 lock-adjacent tests and typecheck stayed green before I reverted.

You are given their hypothesis and the result of the discriminating test they named. You have the repository. Check the claim yourself rather than reasoning about it.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:
- it names a symptom, not the origin: the file where the wrong value is PRINTED rather than where it is computed
- it names the right area but the wrong file, or a set so broad it is not actionable
- the discriminating test does not in fact discriminate: it would pass or fail the same way either way
- the evidence offered does not support the claim, even though the claim may happen to be true

Classify every finding by the evidence you actually have. `reproduced` means you ran something and watched it behave as you describe. `mutation-survived` means you changed a behaviour and the suite stayed green. `narrowed-pin` means a test pins a narrower claim than the requirement behind it. `advisory` is anything you could not evidence at that bar — use it honestly rather than inflating a hunch.

{"adversary":{"description":"Tries to break a proposed root cause, and classifies what it finds by evidence class.","prompt":"You are an adversarial reviewer. Someone has proposed a root cause for a fault, and your job is to find out whether it is actually right.

You are given their hypothesis and the result of the discriminating test they named. You have the repository. Check the claim yourself rather than reasoning about it.

Ways a root cause is wrong, in the order they are usually wrong:
- it names a symptom, not the origin: the file where the wrong value is PRINTED rather than where it is computed
- it names the right area but the wrong file, or a set so broad it is not actionable

AC-016, AC-017 and AC-018 — the three criteria added by review #1 — have no implementation and no test anywhere in src/, test/ or dist/, and all three are reproducibly violated at the CLI level.

The defect and its remaining work sit entirely inside the spec's declared boundary (src/store/verify.ts, test/verify.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md), and the #146 workflow half is inside it too. I cannot score this higher because the fixture is a single squashed commit containing the whole repo, so the story's actual diff cannot be scoped against the declared fence. Against that: zero cases exist for the three review-added ACs, AC-017's own prescribed verification shape (fence/fence) is provably non-discriminating because of the first-fence latch, and AC-014's assertion is a documented narrowing of its criterion.

The AC-017 inversion has no corpus instance today (0 widened pattern sets across 151 specs) but turns any future exclusion list into an allow-list.

root_cause.summary: `sectionPatterns` in src/store/verify.ts shipped the #147 depth-aware terminator (a boundary section now runs to the next same-or-shallower heading) WITHOUT the two guards that bound it: a language-tagged fence (```js) is still read as a path list, and a negation subheading (`Explicitly not in this PR` / `Out of scope`) still contributes its fence and its table to the ALLOWED set. So widening the section manufactures boundaries out of discussed code — flipping a passing advisory into a hard `boundary` failure on the repo's own corpus — and inverts an exclusion list into an allow-list. CHANGELOG.md still carries the compatibility claim ("can only widen … never narrow") that this behaviour falsifies.

hypothesis.summary: Read src/store/verify.ts end to end. The #146 half (STORY_TRAILER, trailerCommits, storyTrailerIds, resolveStoryCommits, provenanceCheck's trailer branch, verifyIdentity's `commits=` input, runVerify's ownScope) is fully present and its tests pass; the AC-014/015 `record-links` instructions are present in workflows/forge-implement.js (2 occurrences). The #147 depth-aware terminator is present too — but grep across src/, test/ and dist/ finds no PATH_FENCE_INFO, NEGATION_SUBHEADING, negatedAt or any negation handling, and no AC-016/AC-017/AC-018 tests exist. I wrote scratch CLI-level tests to discriminate. (a) Copying the real corpus file .bklg/support/fix-lane-plumbing/issue-48-stray-paths-false-fatal/spec.md verbatim into a story makes `boundary` return pass:false: its depth-1 title is the only /boundary/i heading, so the widened section reaches EOF and the ```js fence at lines 30-32 becomes a declared pattern — the advisory→hard-failure flip AC-016 exists to prevent. (c) With the exclusion subheading FIRST, its bare fence consumes the section's single haveFence slot and the boundary inverts to {forbidden/}, making `allowed/x.txt` a stray. The behaviour originates in sectionPatterns/fencePatterns; the changelog line is the same missing deliverable's doc surface.

root_cause.summary: The checklist gate's multi-line GateError diagnostic is discarded at the two places that populate `detail`: `evaluateGate`'s non-blocking checklist catch (`src/process/gates.ts:451`, `detail: err.message.split("\n")[0] ?? ""`) and `previewExitGate`'s catch (`src/process/engine.ts:459`, `detail: err.message.split("\n")[0]`). Both keep only the headline, so the unticked `- [ ]` lines and the "No checked items found in artifact." / "Found checked: ..." note never reach the recorded `gate_result` note or the `advance` dry-run preview sentence. The spec'd fix was never applied to this tree — the truncation is still present, `CHANGELOG.md`'s [Unreleased] is empty, and no regression tests exist.

digest.summary: Read evaluateChecklist (gates.ts:169-181) and confirmed it builds the full message. Confirmed both call sites still truncate, and that the working tree is clean at the pre-fix commit with no CHANGELOG entry, no new tests (15/15 in engine-gates.test.ts, not the reported 18), and an unfilled implementation-report stub — i.e. the reported fix was never landed. Wrote a temporary repro test that seeded a checklist-gated process with 3 unticked boxes: the dry-run printed `Gate 'gates/chk' would BLOCK: checklist gate 'gates/chk' failed: 3 required item(s) not ticked:.` naming nothing, and the non-blocking path recorded a truncated `gate_result.note` while stderr showed the full message — isolating the loss to the `detail` assignments rather than to evaluateChecklist or to advance.ts. Patching only gates.ts:451 and engine.ts:459 to `detail: err.message` turned all three ACs (unticked item names in both paths, plus the 'No checked items found in artifact.' note) green with zero change to src/cli/advance.ts; I then reverted the patch and deleted the temp test. The existing dry-run test only asserts /would BLOCK/i, which is why the defect is silent.

findings.claim: The summary's claim that the two `detail` assignments are why the unticked lines "never reach the recorded gate_result note" holds only for the non-blocking path; the blocking path truncates at an unnamed third site, engine.ts:1089-1090 `headline()`.
findings.rationale: I applied the proposed fix in full and then exercised a blocking checklist gate: the recorded gate_result note is still headline-only, so the named sites do not account for that half of the stated symptom. repro.expected_when_met: If the two named sites were the whole cause of the lost gate_result note, the blocking gate's recorded note would contain "- [ ] Record constraints." once they were patched.

rubric.rationale: None of AC-001, AC-002 or AC-003 is met in this tree. Both truncation sites named by the spec are still `err.message.split("\n")[0]`, and fresh tests written directly from the AC text fail at HEAD: the preview sentence reproduces the issue's `not ticked:.` verbatim, and the non-blocking gate_result note carries only the headline.

The working tree is clean at the pre-fix commit — `git status --short` is empty and `git diff --stat` shows nothing. No file inside or outside the spec's frozen boundary (gates.ts, engine.ts, test/engine-gates.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md) has been modified, so nothing strayed. Full marks here reflect only that nothing was touched, not that work was done correctly.

No regression tests exist: engine-gates.test.ts has 15 tests, and the sole preview test asserts `/would BLOCK/i` — a predicate that is true whether or not the diagnostic names any item. The implementation-report's TDD evidence table is an empty stub with no AC rows. The named discriminating test passes identically in both states, so it provides no signal at all.

Zero source changes exist, so no regression can have been introduced. I additionally confirmed the corrective patch itself is low risk: the other `detail` producers in gates.ts (command-gate paths ~297-381) already carry full messages and were untouched, and the full suite stayed green with the patch applied, matching AC-004's byte-for-byte requirement for other gate types.

The working tree is clean at the pre-fix commit — `git status --short` is empty and `git diff --stat` shows nothing. The declared merge gate is genuinely green: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and `npx vitest run` reports 91/91 files and 1848/1848 tests passing. It is also green after the corrective patch, which is precisely why greenness here is uninformative about the defect rather than evidence against it.

I additionally confirmed the corrective patch itself is low risk: the other `detail` producers in gates.ts (command-gate paths ~297-381) already carry full messages and were untouched, and the full suite stayed green with the patch applied, matching AC-004's byte-for-byte requirement for other gate types.

root_cause.summary: The checklist gate's multi-line GateError diagnostic is discarded at the two places that populate `detail`: `evaluateGate`'s non-blocking checklist catch (`src/process/gates.ts:451`, `detail: err.message.split("\n")[0] ?? ""`) and `previewExitGate`'s catch (`src/process/engine.ts:459`, `detail: err.message.split("\n")[0]`). Both keep only the headline, so the unticked `- [ ]` lines and the "No checked items found in artifact." / "Found checked: ..." note never reach the recorded `gate_result` note or the `advance` dry-run preview sentence. The spec'd fix was never applied to this tree — the truncation is still present, `CHANGELOG.md`'s [Unreleased] is empty, and no regression tests exist.

hypothesis.summary: Read evaluateChecklist (gates.ts:169-181) and confirmed it builds the full message. Confirmed both call sites still truncate, and that the working tree is clean at the pre-fix commit with no CHANGELOG entry, no new tests (15/15 in engine-gates.test.ts, not the reported 18), and an unfilled implementation-report stub — i.e. the reported fix was never landed. Wrote a temporary repro test that seeded a checklist-gated process with 3 unticked boxes: the dry-run printed `Gate 'gates/chk' would BLOCK: checklist gate 'gates/chk' failed: 3 required item(s) not ticked:.` naming nothing, and the non-blocking path recorded a truncated `gate_result.note` while stderr showed the full message — isolating the loss to the `detail` assignments rather than to evaluateChecklist or to advance.ts. Patching only gates.ts:451 and engine.ts:459 to `detail: err.message` turned all three ACs (unticked item names in both paths, plus the 'No checked items found in artifact.' note) green with zero change to src/cli/advance.ts; I then reverted the patch and deleted the temp test. The existing dry-run test only asserts /would BLOCK/i, which is why the defect is silent.

digest.discriminating_test: test/plan-contract.test.ts (AC-001: the "## Companions" instruction slice of workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js must not match /_plan\.md/) and test/plan-dag.test.ts (AC-002/AC-003: a "link-plan" dispatch exists iff the latest verdict.planWritten === true)

root_cause.summary: The RK-S0225 fix was never actually applied to the code: `workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js`'s Stage 1 project-charter prompt (lines 714-715) still instructs the agent to author a Companions link to `${DIR}/_plan.md` — a rollup only Stage B-2 writes — so every charter carries a guaranteed-dead relative link that the same run's Stage 5 dead-anchor check (item 4) resolves and flags; and `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` still has no `planWritten`-gated step that appends the `../_plan.md` companion link to each project's `project.md` once the rollup genuinely exists.

digest.summary: I read the two named workflows rather than trusting the implementation report. `workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js:714-715` still reads "...up to the initiative ${INITIATIVE_PATH} and the rollup ${DIR}/_plan.md" — the exact text AC-001 says must be gone; Stage 5's dead-anchor check (lines 941-946) resolves relative links in any artifact under the project dir against the citing file's own directory, so `project.md`'s `../_plan.md` is a self-inflicted deadAnchor in the same run. `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` has `PLAN_PATH` (371) and `projectItemPath` (374) but, between the `verdict = reVerdict` reassignment and the Manifest block (~1262-1277), there is no new gated step at all: a repo-wide grep for `link-plan` (excluding .git/node_modules) returns nothing, `workflows/_lib/tiers.mjs` has no `link-plan` TIER_POLICY entry, and `project.md` is still only READ (line 858), never edited. The claimed tests are absent too: the report cites 35 tests in test/plan-contract.test.ts and 28 in test/plan-dag.test.ts, but `npx vitest run` on those files gives 34 and 25 — precisely the pre-fix counts (missing the 1 + 3 new AC-001/AC-002/AC-003/EC-001 cases), and CHANGELOG.md has no #74 entry. As direct evidence I added a throwaway probe test asserting AC-001's content contract and the existence of a link-plan dispatch; both assertions failed against the current tree (probe deleted, working tree clean). The delivery is a silent no-op — the suite is green only because the tests that would catch it were never written — so the wrong behaviour still originates where the dead link is authored (forge-plan-briefs.js's Stage 1 Companions instruction) and where the compensating post-`planWritten` link step is missing (forge-plan-prds.js).

root_cause.summary: The RK-S0225 fix was never actually applied to the code: `workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js`'s Stage 1 project-charter prompt (lines 714-715) still instructs the agent to author a Companions link to `${DIR}/_plan.md` — a rollup only Stage B-2 writes — so every charter carries a guaranteed-dead relative link that the same run's Stage 5 dead-anchor check (item 4) resolves and flags; and `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` still has no `planWritten`-gated step that appends the `../_plan.md` companion link to each project's `project.md` once the rollup genuinely exists.

structured_output.summary: I read the two named workflows rather than trusting the implementation report. `workflows/forge-plan-briefs.js:714-715` still reads "...up to the initiative ${INITIATIVE_PATH} and the rollup ${DIR}/_plan.md" — the exact text AC-001 says must be gone; Stage 5's dead-anchor check (lines 941-946) resolves relative links in any artifact under the project dir against the citing file's own directory, so `project.md`'s `../_plan.md` is a self-inflicted deadAnchor in the same run. `workflows/forge-plan-prds.js` has `PLAN_PATH` (371) and `projectItemPath` (374) but, between the `verdict = reVerdict` reassignment and the Manifest block (~1262-1277), there is no new gated step at all: a repo-wide grep for `link-plan` (excluding .git/node_modules) returns nothing, `workflows/_lib/tiers.mjs` has no `link-plan` TIER_POLICY entry, and `project.md` is still only READ (line 858), never edited. The delivery is a silent no-op — the suite is green only because the tests that would catch it were never written — so the wrong behaviour still originates where the dead link is authored (forge-plan-briefs.js's Stage 1 Companions instruction) and where the compensating post-`planWritten` link step is missing (forge-plan-prds.js).

findings.claim: commands/plan.md step 9 still has no sub-step authoring discover.md or ticking the four `## Gate: Discover` boxes, so the literal instruction it gives for a standard-tier story fails on the gates/discover checklist gate.
findings.rationale: I did not reason about the gate — I drove the real CLI. Scaffolded a scratch repo, created a standard-tier story with the exact `redkiln new story` flags step 9 dictates (no --process story-lite), inspected the rendered discover.md (all four boxes unticked), ran the literal advance and watched it exit 1. I then ran the counterfactual: ticking the four boxes made the identical command exit 0, which proves the origin is the missing instruction and not the gate engine or processes/story.yaml. root_cause.summary: None of the RK-S0232 fix landed. The wrong behaviour still originates in the six commands/*.md files, whose "Invoking the workflow" note and every `scriptPath` placeholder still resolve the unset `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` (12 live matches), because the routing-around mechanism was never written: `bundledWorkflowsDir()` is absent from src/store/paths.ts, src/cli/workflow-root.ts does not exist, and `workflow-root` is registered in neither the COMMANDS array nor the dispatch switch.

digest.summary:
The RK-S0232 implementation never landed — none of the frozen-boundary changes exist in the tree, despite an implementation report claiming red→green TDD, three clean gates, and specific line numbers.

Direct evidence: (1) `node bin/redkiln.mjs workflow-root` prints "redkiln: unknown command 'workflow-root'" and exits 1; (2) `grep -rn CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT commands/` still returns 12 matches across all six files — the shared "Invoking the workflow" note plus every `scriptPath: '<$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>/workflows/forge-*.js'` placeholder — directly contradicting AC-003; (3) `src/store/paths.ts` exports only `bundledProcessesDir`/`bundledTemplatesDir`/`bundledKbSkeletonDir`, no `bundledWorkflowsDir` (the report's cited `paths.ts:52-70` is actually `bundledKbSkeletonDir`); (4) `src/cli/workflow-root.ts` does not exist, `COMMANDS` in `src/cli/commands.ts` ends at `record-links`, and `src/cli/index.ts`'s dispatch switch has no `case "workflow-root"`; (5) `test/workflow-root.test.ts` does not exist; (6) `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli.mdx` jumps from `## record-links` to `## See also`; (7) `CHANGELOG.md`'s `[Unreleased]` has only `### Fixed`, no `Added` entry naming #70; (8) `dist/cli.js` contains zero occurrences of `workflow-root`, so the claimed `pnpm build` did not happen either.

The tree is a single clean commit ("advance to implement") with no stash, no second branch, and no worktree, so this is omission, not loss.

Why it went unnoticed: `test/flag-projection.test.ts` is table-driven over the `COMMANDS` array, so a MISSING entry yields no test case rather than a failing one; and `index.ts`'s `name satisfies never` exhaustiveness guard only fires when a name is added to `COMMANDS`. I ran the suite — 69 tests, all green, with no `workflow-root` case. Nothing in the repo can observe an absent command, so the full gate stays green while the fix is entirely missing.

Consequently the original #70 defect is untouched: the six commands/*.md files still instruct the orchestrator to resolve $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which is empty in both shell tools, so the workflow-launch step remains unfollowable and the only recoveries are the two the paragraph forbids.

root_cause.summary: None of the RK-S0232 fix landed. The wrong behaviour still originates in the six commands/*.md files, whose "Invoking the workflow" note and every `scriptPath` placeholder still resolve the unset `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` (12 live matches), because the routing-around mechanism was never written: `bundledWorkflowsDir()` is absent from src/store/paths.ts, src/cli/workflow-root.ts does not exist, and `workflow-root` is registered in neither the COMMANDS array nor the dispatch switch.

hypothesis.summary:
The RK-S0232 implementation never landed — none of the frozen-boundary changes exist in the tree, despite an implementation report claiming red→green TDD, three clean gates, and specific line numbers.

Direct evidence: (1) `node bin/redkiln.mjs workflow-root` prints "redkiln: unknown command 'workflow-root'" and exits 1; (2) `grep -rn CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT commands/` still returns 12 matches across all six files — the shared "Invoking the workflow" note plus every `scriptPath: '<$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>/workflows/forge-*.js'` placeholder — directly contradicting AC-003; (3) `src/store/paths.ts` exports only `bundledProcessesDir`/`bundledTemplatesDir`/`bundledKbSkeletonDir`, no `bundledWorkflowsDir` (the report's cited `paths.ts:52-70` is actually `bundledKbSkeletonDir`); (4) `src/cli/workflow-root.ts` does not exist, `COMMANDS` in `src/cli/commands.ts` ends at `record-links`, and `src/cli/index.ts`'s dispatch switch has no `case "workflow-root"`; (5) `test/workflow-root.test.ts` does not exist; (6) `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli.mdx` jumps from `## record-links` to `## See also`; (7) `CHANGELOG.md`'s `[Unreleased]` has only `### Fixed`, no `Added` entry naming #70; (8) `dist/cli.js` contains zero occurrences of `workflow-root`, so the claimed `pnpm build` did not happen either.

The tree is a single clean commit ("advance to implement") with no stash, no second branch, and no worktree, so this is omission, not loss.

Why it went unnoticed: `test/flag-projection.test.ts` is table-driven over the `COMMANDS` array, so a MISSING entry yields no test case rather than a failing one; and `index.ts`'s `name satisfies never` exhaustiveness guard only fires when a name is added to `COMMANDS`. I ran the suite — 69 tests, all green, with no `workflow-root` case. Nothing in the repo can observe an absent command, so the full gate stays green while the fix is entirely missing.

Consequently the original #70 defect is untouched: the six commands/*.md files still instruct the orchestrator to resolve $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which is empty in both shell tools, so the workflow-launch step remains unfollowable and the only recoveries are the two the paragraph forbids.
